55570.q: Roughly how many people live in the Republic of Ireland (as of 2025)?
55570.e: In 2025 about 5.5 million people lived in the Republic of Ireland. That is clearly fewer than in Switzerland with about 9 million.
55570.m: Ireland has clearly fewer inhabitants than Switzerland.

55571.q: What are the areas of Ireland called where Irish is still the everyday language?
55571.e: The Gaeltacht lies mainly on the west coast, for example in Donegal and Galway. There Irish is spoken in families and schools.
55571.m: In the Gaeltacht, Irish is spoken in everyday life.

55572.q: Which oldest university in Ireland stands in the centre of Dublin?
55572.e: Trinity College was founded in 1592. It is the oldest university in Ireland.
55572.m: Trinity College in Dublin is Ireland's oldest university.

55573.q: Where does the Ha'penny Bridge in Dublin get its name from?
55573.e: Anyone who wanted to cross the footbridge from 1816 had to pay half a penny. That is where the name Ha'penny Bridge comes from.
55573.m: Crossing the Ha'penny Bridge used to cost half a penny.

55574.q: How do trains travel between England and France across the English Channel today?
a: Through a tunnel under the sea
55574.e: The Channel Tunnel has linked England and France since 1994. It is about 50 kilometres long.
55574.m: A railway tunnel runs under the English Channel.

55575.q: Which largest island of England lies in the English Channel off Southampton?
55575.e: The Isle of Wight lies off the south coast of England. It is the largest island that belongs to England.
55575.m: The Isle of Wight is England's largest island.

55576.q: Which two countries does the Channel Tunnel link?
55576.e: The Channel Tunnel has linked England with France since 1994. Trains run directly from London to Paris.
55576.m: The Channel Tunnel links Great Britain with France.

55577.q: What travels through the Channel Tunnel?
55577.e: Only trains travel through the Channel Tunnel. Cars and lorries are loaded onto special car trains.
55577.m: Only trains travel through the Channel Tunnel.

55578.q: How was the Channel Tunnel built?
a: With boring machines from both sides
55578.e: Large tunnel boring machines dug towards each other from England and from France. They met under the sea in 1990.
55578.m: The Channel Tunnel was bored from both sides.

55579.q: Which record does the Channel Tunnel hold?
a: Longest undersea section of any railway tunnel
Longest road tunnel in the world
55579.e: About 38 kilometres of the Channel Tunnel lie under the sea. No other railway tunnel has such a long section under water.
55579.m: The Channel Tunnel has the longest undersea section in the world.

55580.q: Roughly how long does the car train journey through the Channel Tunnel take?
55580.e: The shuttle train takes about 35 minutes from terminal to terminal. The crossing by ferry takes much longer.
55580.m: You travel through the Channel Tunnel in about half an hour.

55581.q: What does the English word “henge” mean for structures like Stonehenge?
a: A round area with a ditch and bank
A stone wall around a village
55581.e: A henge is a circular site from the New Stone Age, surrounded by an earth bank and a ditch. Stonehenge has such a circular ditch.
55581.m: A henge is a round area with a bank and a ditch.

55582.q: What type of rock are the big sarsen stones of Stonehenge made of?
55582.e: The big stones are sarsens, a very hard sandstone. They come from the area around Marlborough, about 25 kilometres to the north.
55582.m: The big stones of Stonehenge are made of hard sandstone.

55583.q: Like Stonehenge, Avebury in England is known for something from the Stone Age. What?
55583.e: Avebury has the largest stone circle in Europe. It even surrounds parts of the village and, like Stonehenge, is a World Heritage Site.
55583.m: Europe's largest stone circle is at Avebury.

55584.q: In which French region does the Seine rise?
55584.e: The Seine rises on the Langres Plateau in Burgundy. From there it flows north-west through Paris to the sea.
55584.m: The source of the Seine is in Burgundy.

55585.q: Near which port does the Seine flow into the sea?
55585.e: The Seine flows into the sea through a wide estuary near Le Havre and Honfleur. Le Havre is one of the most important ports in France.
55585.m: The Seine reaches the sea at Le Havre.

55586.q: Which city does the Seine flow through?
55586.e: The Seine flows right through Paris. Just before the city, the Marne, its longest tributary, joins it.

55588.q: Which famous cathedral stands on the Île de la Cité, an island in the Seine?
55588.e: Notre-Dame Cathedral stands on the Île de la Cité in the middle of Paris. After the fire of 2019 it reopened in 2024.
55588.m: Notre-Dame stands on an island in the Seine.

55589.q: On which hill in the north of Paris does the Sacré-Cœur Basilica stand?
55589.e: The white Sacré-Cœur Basilica stands on Montmartre, the highest hill in Paris. The area used to be a well-known meeting place for painters.
55589.m: Sacré-Cœur sits on top of Montmartre.

55590.q: Which monument stands at the top end of the Avenue des Champs-Élysées?
55590.e: The Arc de Triomphe stands on the Place Charles-de-Gaulle at the top end of the Champs-Élysées. Napoleon had it built from 1806.
55590.m: The Arc de Triomphe crowns the Champs-Élysées.

55591.q: Which is the longest river in France?
55591.e: The Loire is about 1000 kilometres long and flows only through France. It rises in the Massif Central.
55591.m: The Loire is the longest river in France.

55592.q: Roughly how long is the Loire?
55592.e: The Loire is about 1000 kilometres long. It flows entirely through France.
55592.m: The Loire is roughly a thousand kilometres long.

55593.q: Into which sea does the Loire flow?
55593.e: The Loire flows west and reaches the Atlantic at Saint-Nazaire.
55593.m: The Loire flows into the Atlantic.

55594.q: Which of these cities lies on the Loire?
55594.e: Tours lies in the middle of the Loire Valley. Lyon is on the Rhône and Saône, Rouen on the Seine and Toulouse on the Garonne.
55594.m: Tours is a city on the Loire.

55595.q: What is the Loire Valley especially famous for?
55595.e: In the Loire Valley, kings and nobles built magnificent châteaux such as Chambord. That is why it is also called the “Valley of the Kings”.
55595.m: The Loire Valley is known for its châteaux.

55596.q: What grows in large amounts on the slopes of the Loire Valley?
55596.e: The mild climate of the Loire Valley is well suited to growing wine. Vegetables and fruit also grow well there.
55596.m: A lot of wine is grown in the Loire Valley.

55597.q: In which mountains does the Loire rise?
55597.e: The Loire and its tributary the Allier come from the Massif Central, an old volcanic range in the middle of France.
55597.m: The Loire rises in the Massif Central.

55598.q: In which country does the Garonne rise?
55598.e: The Garonne rises in the Val d'Aran in the Spanish Pyrenees. Only after that does it flow into France.
55598.m: The Garonne has its source in Spain.

55599.q: Which city on the Garonne is called the “Ville rose” because of its brick buildings?
55599.e: Toulouse is known for its reddish brick buildings. That is why it is called “the pink city” in French.
55599.m: Toulouse is the pink city on the Garonne.

55600.q: Which port city on the Garonne is world-famous for its wine?
55600.e: Bordeaux lies on the Garonne and is the centre of one of the best-known wine regions in the world. Its old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
55600.m: Bordeaux is a wine city on the Garonne.

55601.q: What is the name of the estuary that the Garonne and Dordogne form together?
55601.e: North of Bordeaux the Garonne and the Dordogne meet. Together they form the Gironde, one of the largest estuaries in Europe.
55601.m: The Garonne and Dordogne together form the Gironde.

55602.q: Which canal links the Garonne at Toulouse with the Mediterranean?
55602.e: The Canal du Midi was built in the 17th century and runs from Toulouse to the Mediterranean. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
55602.m: The Canal du Midi links Toulouse with the Mediterranean.

55603.q: Which industry is especially important in Toulouse on the Garonne?
55603.e: Many aircraft are built and satellites developed in Toulouse. The city is a European centre of the aerospace industry.
55603.m: Toulouse is a city of aircraft and satellites.

55604.q: What is the mascaret on the Garonne?
a: A tidal wave that travels upstream
55604.e: At a strong high tide the sea pushes water into the Gironde and creates a wave that travels upstream. Some surfers ride it.
55604.m: The mascaret is a tidal wave that travels upstream.

55605.q: In which country is the Massif Central?
55605.e: The Massif Central is an upland area in the south of France. Its highest peak, the Puy de Sancy, is about 1886 metres high.
55605.m: The Massif Central is in France.

55606.q: What are the many round mountains of the Chaîne des Puys in the Massif Central?
55606.e: The Chaîne des Puys is made up of about 80 extinct volcanoes. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2018.
55606.m: The Chaîne des Puys is a chain of extinct volcanoes.

55607.q: Which region in the Massif Central is known for its old volcanoes?
55607.e: There are many extinct volcanoes in the Auvergne, for example the Puy de Dôme near Clermont-Ferrand.
55607.m: The Auvergne is France's volcano country.

55608.q: What is the Millau Viaduct in France famous for?
a: It is one of the highest bridges in the world
It is the longest tunnel in the world
It is the oldest Roman bridge
55608.e: The Millau Viaduct opened in 2004 and crosses the valley of the Tarn. With its tallest mast it is even higher than the Eiffel Tower.
55608.m: The Millau Viaduct is one of the highest bridges in the world.

55609.q: Which blue cheese made from sheep's milk ripens in caves on the southern edge of the Massif Central?
55609.e: Roquefort ripens in the limestone caves of Roquefort-sur-Soulzon. There, cool air currents keep the climate even.

55610.q: Is the Massif Central older or younger than the Alps?
55610.e: The Massif Central is an ancient, worn-down range that formed over 300 million years ago. The Alps are much younger and therefore higher and more rugged.
55610.m: The Massif Central is much older than the Alps.

55611.q: Which pilgrims' route starts in Le Puy-en-Velay in the Massif Central?
55611.e: The Via Podiensis leads from Le Puy-en-Velay towards Santiago de Compostela. It is one of the most important French routes of the Way of St James.
55611.m: A well-known Way of St James starts in Le Puy-en-Velay.

55612.q: Between which two countries do the Pyrenees form the border?
55612.e: The Pyrenees separate France in the north from Spain in the south. The small country of Andorra lies in the middle of the mountains.
55612.m: The Pyrenees separate France and Spain.

55613.q: What shaped the huge rock bowl of the Cirque de Gavarnie in the Pyrenees?
55613.e: In the Ice Age, glaciers carved out the bowl with its steep walls. Today a high waterfall plunges down there.
55613.m: The Cirque de Gavarnie was shaped by glaciers.

55614.q: Which Pyrenean pass is especially famous in the Tour de France?
55614.e: The Col du Tourmalet is over 2100 metres high. It has been ridden very often in the Tour de France since 1910.
55614.m: The Col du Tourmalet is a legendary Tour de France pass.

55615.q: Which place of pilgrimage lies on the northern edge of the Pyrenees?
55615.e: Lourdes is one of the largest places of pilgrimage in the world. Every year millions of pilgrims visit the grotto.
55615.m: Lourdes lies at the foot of the Pyrenees.

55616.q: Roughly how long are the Pyrenees?
55616.e: The Pyrenees stretch for about 430 kilometres. They reach from the Bay of Biscay to the Mediterranean.
55616.m: The Pyrenees are about 430 kilometres long.

55617.q: What stands on the summit of the Pic du Midi in the Pyrenees?
55617.e: An observatory has stood on the Pic du Midi de Bigorre since the 19th century. Because the mountain air is clear, it is a good place to watch the stars.
55617.m: There is an observatory on the Pic du Midi.

55618.e: The Iberian Plate pushed against the Eurasian Plate. The rock was squeezed together and folded up into mountains.
55618.m: The Pyrenees are fold mountains from a plate collision.

55619.q: Which purple-flowering plant colours many fields in Provence in summer?
55619.e: A lot of lavender is grown on high plateaus such as the Plateau de Valensole. Fragrant oil is made from the flowers.
55619.m: Lavender blooms in Provence in summer.

55620.q: In which city in Provence did the popes live in the 14th century?
55620.e: From 1309 to 1377 the popes lived in Avignon instead of Rome. The mighty Palace of the Popes still reminds us of this today.
55620.m: Avignon was the city of the popes in the 14th century.

55621.q: What is the name of the strong, cold north wind in the Rhône Valley and Provence?
55621.e: The mistral blows down the Rhône Valley to the Mediterranean. It usually brings clear, sunny but cool weather.
55621.m: The mistral is the cold wind of Provence.

55622.q: Who founded the city of Marseille around 600 BC?
55622.e: Greeks from Phocaea founded the city around 600 BC under the name Massalia. Marseille is considered the oldest city in France.

55623.q: Which area in the Rhône delta is known for flamingos and white horses?
55623.e: The Camargue lies between the arms of the Rhône's mouth. Flamingos live in the lagoons, and half-wild white horses and black bulls on the pastures.
55623.m: Flamingos and white horses live in the Camargue.

55624.q: Which deep gorge in Provence is known for its turquoise water?
55624.e: The River Verdon has cut a gorge up to about 700 metres deep. It is considered one of the largest gorges in Europe.
55624.m: The Verdon Gorge glows turquoise blue.

55625.q: Which mountain in Provence is called the “Giant of Provence”?
55625.e: Mont Ventoux is about 1900 metres high and stands alone above the landscape. Its pale, bare summit can be seen from far away.
55625.m: Mont Ventoux is the Giant of Provence.

55626.q: Which prize is awarded for the best film at the Cannes Film Festival?
55626.e: The top prize at Cannes is the Palme d'Or, the Golden Palm. The Golden Leopard, on the other hand, is awarded at the Locarno Film Festival.
55626.m: The winning film at Cannes receives the Palme d'Or.

55629.q: Which small country lies on the Côte d'Azur?
55629.e: Monaco lies right by the sea between Nice and the Italian border. It is the second smallest country in the world.
55629.m: Monaco lies on the Côte d'Azur.

55630.q: What does “Côte d'Azur” mean in English?
55630.e: Azure is a light, bright blue. The name recalls the colour of the sea and the sky.

55631.q: What is the town of Grasse on the Côte d'Azur world-famous for?
55631.e: For centuries, flowers such as roses and jasmine have been grown in Grasse for fragrances. The town is considered the world capital of perfume.
55631.m: Grasse is the town of perfumes.

55632.q: Why did many famous painters live on the Côte d'Azur?
a: Because of the bright light and mild climate
Because of the many snowy days
Because of the big art schools in the mountains
55632.e: The clear light and bright colours drew painters such as Henri Matisse and Pablo Picasso to the Côte d'Azur.
55632.m: The light of the Côte d'Azur attracted many painters.

55634.q: Which famous French emperor was born on Corsica?
55634.e: Napoleon was born in Ajaccio on Corsica in 1769. Later he became Emperor of the French.

55635.q: What is the dense, fragrant scrubland that covers large parts of Corsica called?
55635.e: The maquis is made up of evergreen shrubs such as strawberry tree, myrtle and rockrose. It smells strongly of herbs.
55635.m: The maquis is Corsica's fragrant scrubland.

55636.e: Corsica lies in the Mediterranean between France and Italy. It is one of the large Mediterranean islands.
55636.m: Corsica is an island in the Mediterranean.

55637.q: What is the landscape like in the interior of Corsica?
55637.e: Corsica is very mountainous. Many mountains are over 2000 metres high, the highest over 2700 metres.

55638.q: What is the climate like on the coasts of Corsica?
55638.e: On the coasts of Corsica the summers are hot and dry, the winters mild and damp.

55639.q: How do most people travel from mainland France to Corsica?
55639.e: Corsica is an island with no bridge or tunnel to the mainland. Ferries go, for example, to Bastia, Ajaccio and Calvi.
55639.m: You get to Corsica by ship or plane.

55640.q: Which language family does Breton belong to?
55640.e: Breton is closely related to Cornish and Welsh. It came to Brittany with settlers from Britain.

55641.q: What is Carnac in Brittany famous for?
55641.e: Near Carnac about 3000 standing stones are arranged in long rows. They were put up in the New Stone Age.
55641.m: There are ancient rows of stones near Carnac.

a: In the north-west of France on the Atlantic
In the south of France on the Mediterranean
In the east of France on the Swiss border
On an island in the Mediterranean
55642.e: Brittany is a peninsula in the north-west of France. It is surrounded by sea on three sides.
55642.m: Brittany is in the north-west of France.

55643.q: What does the tidal power station in Brittany use to produce electricity?
55643.e: In Brittany the sea rises and falls a lot. The power station on the Rance uses the water flowing in and out.
55643.m: A tidal power station uses the tides.

55644.q: What does the name of the Breton département Finistère mean?
55644.e: Finistère comes from the Latin “finis terrae”. It is the westernmost part of France.
55644.m: Finistère means end of the earth.

55645.q: Which flour is the savoury Breton galette made from?
55645.e: The galette is a thin pancake made from buckwheat flour. It is often filled with ham, cheese and egg.
55645.m: A Breton galette is made from buckwheat.

55646.q: What happened on the coast of Normandy on “D-Day” in 1944?
55646.e: On 6 June 1944 Allied troops landed on five beaches in Normandy. It was the beginning of the liberation of Western Europe in the Second World War.
55646.m: On D-Day the Allies landed in Normandy.

55647.q: Which event does the famous Bayeux Tapestry show?
55647.e: The tapestry, about 70 metres long, tells the story of the conquest of England in 1066 in pictures. It is almost 1000 years old.
55647.m: The Bayeux Tapestry tells the story of 1066.

55648.q: Which Duke of Normandy became King of England in 1066?
55648.e: William won the Battle of Hastings in 1066. After that he was crowned King of England.
55648.m: William the Conqueror came from Normandy.

55649.q: Which soft cheese comes from Normandy?
55649.e: Camembert is named after a village in Normandy. The region is known for dairy farming, butter and cream.
55649.m: Camembert is a cheese from Normandy.

55650.q: Which painter created the garden with the famous water lily pond at Giverny?
55650.e: Claude Monet lived in Giverny from 1883. He painted his water lily pond in many large pictures.
55650.m: Monet painted the water lilies in his garden at Giverny.

55651.q: Where does Normandy get its name from?
55651.e: In the 10th century, Vikings from the north settled on the Seine. They were called Normans, meaning “Northmen”.
55651.m: Normandy is named after the Normans.

55652.q: What form of state does Belgium have?
55652.e: Belgium is a kingdom. The country has had a king since 1831, but his duties are mainly ceremonial.

55653.q: Where was Napoleon finally defeated in 1815?
55653.e: The Battle of Waterloo took place south of Brussels. Afterwards Napoleon was exiled to the island of St Helena.
55653.m: Napoleon's rule ended at Waterloo in Belgium.

55654.q: What is the Dutch-speaking north of Belgium called?
55654.e: Flanders, where people speak Dutch, is in the north of Belgium. In Wallonia in the south, people speak French.
55654.m: Flanders is the Dutch-speaking part of Belgium.

55655.q: In which part of Belgium does the German-speaking Community live?
a: In the east on the German border
In the west on the coast
In the south on the French border
55655.e: The German-speaking Community is around Eupen and Sankt Vith in the east of the country. About 80,000 people live there.
55655.m: German is spoken in the east of Belgium.

55656.q: Which comic characters did the Belgian artist Hergé create?
55656.e: From 1929 Hergé drew the adventures of Tintin and his dog Snowy. They have been translated into many languages.

55657.q: Which Belgian city with a medieval old town and canals lies near the North Sea coast?
55657.e: The old town of Bruges is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In the Middle Ages Bruges was a rich trading city.
55657.m: Bruges is a canal city in Belgium.

55658.q: What is the name of the wooded uplands in the south-east of Belgium?
55658.e: The Ardennes stretch from Belgium into Luxembourg and France. They are marked by forests and deep river valleys.
55658.m: The Ardennes are in the south-east of Belgium.

55659.q: Which military alliance has its headquarters in Brussels?
55659.e: NATO's headquarters is in Brussels. That makes the city an important place in international politics.
55659.m: NATO has its headquarters in Brussels.

55660.q: Which Dutch city has the largest seaport in Europe?
55660.e: The port of Rotterdam is the largest in Europe. From here, goods are shipped up the Rhine as far as Basel.
55660.m: Rotterdam has the largest port in Europe.

55661.q: Who is King of the Netherlands (as of 2026)?
55661.e: Willem-Alexander has been King of the Netherlands since 2013. He succeeded his mother Beatrix.
55661.m: Willem-Alexander is King of the Netherlands.

55662.q: Which three rivers together form the large delta in the Netherlands?
55662.e: The Rhine, Meuse and Scheldt flow into the North Sea together through a large delta. The Rhine also brings water from Switzerland.
55662.m: The Rhine, Meuse and Scheldt form a shared delta.

55663.q: Which UN court has its seat in the Peace Palace in The Hague?
55663.e: The International Court of Justice decides disputes between states. It meets in the Peace Palace in The Hague.
55663.m: The International Court of Justice sits in The Hague.

55664.q: Which island in the Caribbean belongs to the Kingdom of the Netherlands?
55664.e: Aruba, Curaçao and Sint Maarten are separate countries within the Kingdom of the Netherlands. Martinique, on the other hand, belongs to France.
55664.m: Aruba belongs to the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

55665.q: What did the Dutch East India Company mainly trade in?
55665.e: The East India Company, or VOC for short, was founded in 1602 and brought spices such as pepper and nutmeg from Asia to Europe. It made the Netherlands rich.
55665.m: The VOC traded in spices from Asia.

55667.q: Which means of transport is especially popular in Amsterdam?
55667.e: Amsterdam is flat and has many cycle paths. There are more bicycles in the city than inhabitants.

55668.q: What do many old houses in Amsterdam stand on, because the ground is soft?
55668.e: Under Amsterdam there is soft, wet peat and clay. So many old houses rest on long wooden piles that reach down to firm layers of sand.
55668.m: Old houses in Amsterdam stand on wooden piles.

a: Land enclosed by dykes and drained
55669.e: A polder is a low-lying area surrounded by dykes. The water is pumped out all the time so that the land stays dry.
55669.m: A polder is land enclosed by dykes and drained.

55670.q: Which lake was created when the Afsluitdijk separated the Zuiderzee from the sea in 1932?
55670.e: The Afsluitdijk cut the Zuiderzee off from the North Sea. Over time the salty arm of the sea became the freshwater lake IJsselmeer.

55671.q: Why was the long Afsluitdijk built in the Netherlands?
a: To protect the land from the sea
As a dam for a power station
55671.e: Large parts of the Netherlands lie below sea level. The Afsluitdijk, about 32 km long, holds back the North Sea and protects the land from storm floods.
55671.m: Dykes protect the Netherlands from the sea.

55672.q: What did the Dutch turn large parts of the Zuiderzee bay into?
55672.e: With dykes and pumps, the seabed was drained. This created Flevoland, which became the twelfth province of the Netherlands in 1986.
55672.m: Flevoland was created on the seabed.

55673.q: Which protection project did the Netherlands build after the great storm flood of 1953?
55673.e: Over 1800 people died in the storm flood of 1953. Afterwards the Delta Works were built, a system of dams, locks and storm surge barriers.
55673.m: The Delta Works protect the south-west of the Netherlands from storm floods.

55674.q: What is special about Schiphol Airport near Amsterdam?
55674.e: Schiphol lies on the bed of the former lake Haarlemmermeer, which was drained. The airport is a few metres below sea level.

55675.q: Why does the Netherlands need many pumping stations?
a: To pump water out of the polders
55675.e: Polders often lie below sea level. Pumping stations such as the Woudagemaal in Friesland pump the water out so the land stays dry.
55675.m: Pumping stations keep the polders dry.

55676.q: Roughly how far below sea level is the lowest point of the Netherlands?
55676.e: The lowest point is in the Zuidplaspolder near Rotterdam, about 6.7 metres below sea level. Without dykes and pumps it would be under water.
55676.m: The lowest point of the Netherlands is about seven metres below the sea.

55677.q: Which industry made Luxembourg wealthy in the 19th and 20th centuries?
55677.e: In the south of Luxembourg, iron ore was mined and made into steel. The company Arbed was one of the largest steelmakers in the world.

55678.q: Which two languages are official languages in Luxembourg alongside Luxembourgish?
55678.e: Luxembourgish, French and German are the official languages in Luxembourg. Many people switch easily between them in everyday life.

55679.q: Which court of the European Union has its seat in Luxembourg?
a: Court of Justice of the EU
55679.e: The Court of Justice of the European Union sits in Luxembourg. It makes sure that EU law is applied in the same way everywhere.
55679.m: The Court of Justice of the EU sits in Luxembourg.

55680.q: Which river forms part of the border between Luxembourg and Germany?
55680.e: In the south-east, the Moselle separates Luxembourg from Germany. Wine is grown on its slopes.
55680.m: The Moselle is a border river of Luxembourg.

55681.q: Which three countries make up the Benelux Union?
55681.e: The name Benelux is made from the beginnings of Belgium, Nederland and Luxembourg. The three countries have worked closely together since the 1940s.
55681.m: Benelux stands for Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg.

55682.q: What is Luxembourg's economy especially known for?
55682.e: Luxembourg is an important financial centre with many banks and funds.
55682.m: Luxembourg is a major financial centre.

55683.q: Since when has Luxembourg been part of the European Community?
55683.e: In 1951 and 1957 Luxembourg was one of the six founding states of the European Communities. These later developed into the EU.
55683.m: Luxembourg is a founding member of the European Communities.

55684.q: Which German state is the largest by area?
55684.e: With about 70,500 square kilometres, Bavaria is the largest state in Germany. That makes it bigger than the whole of Switzerland.
55684.m: Bavaria is Germany's largest state by area.

55685.q: Which German state has the most inhabitants?
55685.e: About 18 million people live in North Rhine-Westphalia, more than in any other German state. It is densely populated and has many big cities.
55685.m: North Rhine-Westphalia is the most populous German state.

55686.q: Which city is the state capital of Hesse?
55686.e: Hesse's largest city is Frankfurt am Main, but the state capital is Wiesbaden. The state parliament and government are based there.
55686.m: Hesse's capital is Wiesbaden, not Frankfurt.

55687.q: Which three German states are city-states?
55687.e: A city-state is a city that is also a state in its own right. In Germany these are Berlin, Hamburg and Bremen.
55687.m: Berlin, Hamburg and Bremen are both cities and states.

55688.q: Which two cities make up the state of Bremen?
55688.e: The state of Bremen consists of the city of Bremen and the port of Bremerhaven at the mouth of the Weser. Between them lies territory of Lower Saxony.
55688.m: The smallest German state consists of Bremen and Bremerhaven.

55689.e: Schleswig-Holstein is the northernmost German state and lies between the North Sea and the Baltic. In the north it borders Denmark.
55689.m: Schleswig-Holstein is Germany's gateway to Denmark.

55690.e: Berlin is a state in its own right, but it lies like an island in the middle of Brandenburg. Many people commute from Brandenburg to work in Berlin every day.
55690.m: Berlin lies in the middle of Brandenburg.

55691.q: Which record does the Berlin TV Tower at Alexanderplatz hold?
a: It is the tallest structure in Germany
It is the oldest tower in Europe
It is the most leaning tower in the world
It is the only tower made of wood
55691.e: The Berlin TV Tower is 368 metres high and the tallest structure in Germany. It was opened in East Germany in 1969.
55691.m: The Berlin TV Tower is the tallest structure in Germany.

55692.q: In which river is Berlin's Museum Island?
55692.e: Museum Island lies in the Spree in central Berlin. It has five large museums and has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1999.
55692.m: Berlin's Museum Island lies in the Spree.

55693.q: Which city is the second largest in Germany?
55693.e: Hamburg has about 1.9 million inhabitants and is the second largest city in Germany after Berlin. It is also a state in its own right.
55693.m: Hamburg is the second largest city in Germany.

55694.q: What is the name of the river that is dammed into two large lakes in Hamburg?
55694.e: In central Hamburg the Alster is dammed to form the Inner Alster and the Outer Alster. People sail and row on the Outer Alster.
55694.m: Thanks to the Alster, Hamburg has lakes in the middle of the city.

55695.q: In which German state is the Ruhr area?
55695.e: The Ruhr area is in the west of Germany in the state of North Rhine-Westphalia. It is the largest urban area in Germany.
55695.m: The Ruhr area is in North Rhine-Westphalia.

55696.q: Which raw material turned the Ruhr area into a great industrial region?
55696.e: There are large deposits of hard coal under the Ruhr area. With coal and steel, the region became an industrial centre from the 19th century.
55696.m: Coal and steel shaped the Ruhr area.

55697.q: What is the former Zollverein colliery in Essen today?
a: A museum and UNESCO World Heritage Site
55697.e: Coal used to be mined at the Zollverein colliery. Today it is a museum and cultural centre and has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2001.
55697.m: The Zollverein colliery in Essen is a World Heritage Site.

55698.q: Into which river does the Ruhr flow?
55698.e: The Ruhr flows into the Rhine at Duisburg. The river gave the whole Ruhr area its name.
55698.m: The Ruhr flows into the Rhine at Duisburg.

55699.q: What was the Ruhr area in 2010?
a: Host of the Football World Cup
55699.e: In 2010 Essen, representing the whole Ruhr area, was European Capital of Culture. The programme was called RUHR.2010.
55699.m: The Ruhr area was European Capital of Culture in 2010.

55700.q: What happens in the Wadden Sea on the North Sea coast at low tide?
a: Waves rise up to the sky
55700.e: At low tide the water goes out. Then you can walk across the seabed of the Wadden Sea, for example to islands such as Juist or Norderney.
55700.m: At low tide the mudflats are dry.

55701.q: What can you see in the Wadden Sea when the tide is out?
a: The seabed of sand and mud
55701.e: At low tide the water goes out and the seabed is uncovered. At high tide it is under water again.
55701.m: At low tide the mudflats dry out.

55702.q: What are the channels in the mudflats called that still carry water at low tide?
55702.e: Tidal creeks are channels in the mudflats through which water flows out at low tide and in at high tide. On a mudflat walk they are dangerous because the water rises quickly.
55702.m: Tidal creeks are dangerous water channels in the mudflats.

55703.q: Which is the highest mountain in Germany?
55703.e: The Zugspitze is 2962 metres high. It is in the Wetterstein range in the Alps.
55703.m: The Zugspitze is the highest mountain in Germany.

55704.q: On the border of which two countries is the Zugspitze?
55704.e: The border between Bavaria and Tyrol runs over the summit of the Zugspitze.
55704.m: The Zugspitze is on the border with Austria.

55705.q: The Dufourspitze is 4634 metres high, the Zugspitze 2962 metres. How many metres higher is the Dufourspitze?
55705.e: You work out 4634 minus 2962, which is 1672. So the highest mountain in Switzerland is 1672 metres higher than the highest mountain in Germany.
55705.m: The Dufourspitze is 1672 metres higher than the Zugspitze.

55706.q: Which is the largest town on Lake Constance?
55706.e: Konstanz has about 85,000 inhabitants and is the largest town on Lake Constance. It borders directly on Kreuzlingen in the canton of Thurgau.
55706.m: Konstanz is the largest town on Lake Constance.

55708.q: What is the place in Koblenz where the Moselle flows into the Rhine called?
55708.e: The tongue of land between the Rhine and the Moselle is called the Deutsches Eck, the “German Corner”. It is a well-known landmark of Koblenz.
55708.m: The Moselle and the Rhine meet at the Deutsches Eck.

55709.q: In which country does the Moselle rise?
55709.e: The Moselle rises in the Vosges in France. It is about 544 kilometres long in total.
55709.m: The Moselle comes from the Vosges in France.

55710.q: Which town on the Moselle is considered the oldest town in Germany and has a Roman city gate?
55710.e: Trier was founded by the Romans. Its best-known building is the Porta Nigra, a Roman city gate.
55710.m: Trier, with the Porta Nigra, is a Roman town on the Moselle.

55711.q: What is the Moselle Valley especially known for?
55711.e: Wine has been grown on the steep slopes of the Moselle Valley since Roman times. The most important grape variety is Riesling.
55711.m: The Moselle Valley is a famous wine region.

55712.q: Which place on the Moselle gave its name to a European agreement on open borders?
55712.e: The Schengen Agreement was signed in 1985 on a boat on the Moselle near the wine village of Schengen in Luxembourg. Switzerland is part of the Schengen Area today too.
55712.m: The Schengen Agreement is named after a village on the Moselle.

55713.q: Which river, after which a German state is named, flows into the Moselle?
55713.e: The Saar flows through Saarland and joins the Moselle just before Trier. The Main, Neckar and Lahn flow into the Rhine.
55713.m: The Saar flows into the Moselle.

55714.q: What can you often see high above the river in the Moselle Valley?
55714.e: Vines grow on the steep slopes of the Moselle, and old castles such as the Reichsburg in Cochem stand on many hills.
55714.m: There are many castles and vineyards in the Moselle Valley.

55715.q: What is the name of the amusement park in Vienna with the famous giant Ferris wheel from 1897?
55715.e: The Vienna Giant Ferris Wheel in the Prater was built in 1897. It is one of the city's landmarks.
55715.m: The giant Ferris wheel turns in Vienna's Prater.

55716.q: Which international organisation has one of its four main offices in Vienna?
55716.e: Several United Nations organisations are based at the Vienna International Centre, known as UNO City. Other major UN sites are New York, Geneva and Nairobi.
55716.m: Like Geneva, Vienna is an important UN seat.

55717.q: How many countries does Austria border?
55717.e: Austria borders Germany, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia, Italy, Switzerland and Liechtenstein. That makes 8 neighbouring countries.

55718.q: Which river forms the border between Austria and Bavaria between Braunau and Passau?
55718.e: The Inn comes from the Engadine in Switzerland and flows through Tyrol. Between Braunau and Passau it is a border river, and at Passau it flows into the Danube.
55718.m: The Inn is a border river between Austria and Bavaria.

55719.q: On which day does Austria celebrate its national holiday?
55719.e: On 26 October 1955 Austria declared its permanent neutrality. Since 1965 this day has been the national holiday.
55719.m: Austria celebrates its national holiday on 26 October.

55720.q: Which city is the state capital of Vorarlberg?
55720.e: Bregenz lies on the eastern shore of Lake Constance and is the state capital of Vorarlberg. The Bregenz Festival on its lake stage is well known.
55720.m: Bregenz is the capital of Vorarlberg.

55721.q: Which is the largest Austrian state by area?
55721.e: With about 19,200 square kilometres, Lower Austria is the largest state. It surrounds the capital Vienna.
55721.m: Lower Austria is Austria's largest state.

55722.q: Which city is the state capital of Styria and the second largest city in Austria?
55722.e: Graz lies on the Mur and has about 300,000 inhabitants. The old town with the clock tower on the Schlossberg is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
55722.m: Graz is the second largest city in Austria.

55723.q: Which state was the last to join Austria, in 1921?
55723.e: Burgenland previously belonged to Hungary and came to Austria in 1921. It is the easternmost state, and its capital is Eisenstadt.

55724.q: Which city on the Danube is the state capital of Upper Austria?
55724.e: Linz lies on the Danube and is the capital of Upper Austria. It is an important place for industry and culture.
55724.m: Linz is the capital of Upper Austria.

55725.q: Which city is the state capital of Carinthia?
55725.e: Klagenfurt am Wörthersee is the capital of Carinthia, the southernmost state. Its landmark is the Dragon Fountain.
55725.m: Klagenfurt is the capital of Carinthia.

55726.q: Which famous scenic road has crossed the Alps near the Grossglockner since 1935?
55726.e: The Grossglockner High Alpine Road opened in 1935. It links the state of Salzburg with Carinthia and is closed in winter.
55726.m: The Grossglockner High Alpine Road is a famous pass road.

55727.q: What lies at the foot of the Grossglockner?
55727.e: The Pasterze lies at the foot of the Grossglockner. It is the largest glacier in Austria, but it melts a little more every year.
55727.m: Austria's largest glacier lies below the Grossglockner.

55728.q: What does the Salzburg Festival present every summer?
55728.e: The Salzburg Festival has existed since 1920. Every summer it presents opera, theatre and concerts, including the play “Jedermann” (Everyman).
55728.m: The Salzburg Festival is a big music and theatre festival.

55729.q: What shapes the landscape of the Salzkammergut?
55729.e: In the Salzkammergut there are many lakes between high mountains, for example the Attersee, the largest lake lying entirely in Austria.
55729.m: The Salzkammergut is a land of lakes and mountains.

55730.q: Which emperor spent almost every summer in the Salzkammergut?
55730.e: Emperor Franz Joseph, the husband of Empress Sisi, stayed at the Kaiservilla in Bad Ischl in summer.
55730.m: Emperor Franz Joseph spent his summers in Bad Ischl.

55731.q: Which raw material gave the Salzkammergut its name?
55731.e: The “Kammer” was the emperor's treasury, and the salt from this area belonged to it. That is why the region was called the Salzkammergut.
55731.m: The Salzkammergut is named after salt.

55732.q: Which city is the state capital of Lower Saxony?
55732.e: Hanover lies on the Leine and is the seat of the Lower Saxony state parliament. The city is also known for its big trade fair.
55732.m: Hanover is the capital of Lower Saxony.

55733.q: Which is the smallest German state that is not a city-state?
55733.e: With about 2570 square kilometres, Saarland is the smallest non-city state in Germany. It borders France and Luxembourg.
55733.m: Saarland is Germany's smallest non-city state.

55734.q: Which city was the capital of the Federal Republic of Germany (West Germany) until reunification?
55734.e: From 1949 to 1990 Bonn on the Rhine was the capital of the Federal Republic. After reunification, parliament and government moved to Berlin.
55734.m: Before Berlin, Bonn was the capital of West Germany.

55735.q: What is true about the bridges in Berlin?
a: There are more bridges than in Venice
There is not a single bridge
All the bridges are made of wood
55735.e: Because of the Spree, the Havel and many canals, Berlin has well over 1000 bridges. Venice has only about 400.
55735.m: Berlin has more bridges than Venice.

55736.q: Berlin is the capital of Germany. What else is Berlin?
a: A state in its own right
55736.e: Berlin is both a city and a state, like Hamburg and Bremen. It has 12 districts, for example Mitte and Spandau.
55736.m: Berlin is both a city and a state.

55737.q: What did Berlin's BER airport become known for?
a: Being the largest airport in the world
55737.e: BER airport was supposed to open in 2011. Because of many building faults it did not open until October 2020.
55737.m: Berlin's BER airport opened nine years late.

55738.q: Which is the largest seaport in Germany?
55738.e: The port of Hamburg lies on the Elbe, about 100 kilometres from the open sea. It is the largest seaport in Germany and one of the largest container ports in Europe.
55738.m: Hamburg has the largest seaport in Germany.

55739.q: Which medieval league of trading cities did Hamburg belong to, as can still be seen in its official name today?
55739.e: The Hanseatic League was an alliance of merchants and towns on the North Sea and the Baltic. Hamburg's official name is still the “Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg”.

55740.q: What is the name of the tunnel opened in 1911 that lets you walk under the Elbe in Hamburg?
55740.e: The Old Elbe Tunnel links the Landungsbrücken in St. Pauli with the other side of the Elbe. Pedestrians and cyclists go down in large lifts.
55740.m: The Old Elbe Tunnel has run under the Elbe since 1911.

55741.q: Which exhibition in Hamburg's Speicherstadt has the largest model railway in the world?
55741.e: Miniatur Wunderland shows thousands of metres of track with trains, towns and even an airport in miniature. It is one of the most visited sights in Hamburg.
55741.m: Countless little trains run in Miniatur Wunderland.

55745.q: Which border did a section of the Elbe form between 1949 and 1990?
a: The border between West and East Germany
The border between Germany and Poland
The border between Saxony and Bavaria
The border between Germany and Denmark
55745.e: Between Lauenburg and Schnackenburg the Elbe was part of the inner German border. West Germany lay on one side, East Germany on the other.
55745.m: For a stretch, the Elbe was the border between East and West.

55746.q: Which is the largest city in the Ruhr area?
55746.e: Dortmund has just under 600,000 inhabitants and is, just ahead of Essen, the largest city in the Ruhr area. It is also known for its big football club.
55746.m: Dortmund is the largest city in the Ruhr area.

55747.q: Which country does NOT border the North Sea?
55747.e: Poland lies on the Baltic Sea. Germany, the Netherlands and Norway all have a North Sea coast.
55747.m: Poland lies on the Baltic, not on the North Sea.

55748.q: What is the name of the huge sandbank in the middle of the North Sea between England and Denmark?
55748.e: Dogger Bank is a large, shallow sandbank in the North Sea. In the Ice Age it was dry land where people and animals lived.
55748.m: Dogger Bank is a huge sandbank in the North Sea.

55749.q: Which big river flows through Hamburg and into the North Sea?
55749.e: The Elbe comes from the Czech Republic, flows through Hamburg and reaches the North Sea at Cuxhaven. The Danube flows into the Black Sea.
55749.m: The Elbe flows into the North Sea.

55750.q: What do people on the North Sea coast build to protect themselves from storm floods?
55750.e: Dykes are high earth banks along the coast. After the severe storm flood of 1962 in Hamburg they were raised a lot.
55750.m: Dykes protect the coast from storm floods.

55751.q: Which animal often rests on the sandbanks in the Wadden Sea?
55751.e: At low tide seals like to lie on the sandbanks and rest. They also have their young there.
55751.m: Seals live in the Wadden Sea.

55753.q: What is the fine, muddy and often soft ground in the mudflats called?
55753.e: This mud is made of very fine particles and lots of remains of plants and animals. It is full of nutrients, so many worms, shellfish and snails live in it.
55753.m: The soft ground of the mudflats is fine mud.

55754.q: What makes the Wadden Sea unique in the world?
a: It is the largest continuous area of mudflats on Earth
It is the deepest sea in Europe
It is the saltiest sea in the world
It freezes over completely every winter
55754.e: The Wadden Sea stretches from the Netherlands through Germany to Denmark. Nowhere else is there such a large continuous system of sand and mud flats.
55754.m: The Wadden Sea is the largest area of mudflats in the world.

55756.q: How do many visitors get to the summit of the Zugspitze easily?
55756.e: From the Eibsee, the Zugspitze cable car reaches the summit in a few minutes. It has been running since 2017.
55756.m: A cable car goes up the Zugspitze.

55757.q: What is on the Zugspitzplatt below the summit?
55757.e: Germany's highest ski area is on the Zugspitzplatt. Because it is so high, you can often ski there until spring.
55757.m: Germany's highest ski area is on the Zugspitzplatt.

55758.q: How high is the Feldberg, the highest peak in the Black Forest?
55758.e: The Feldberg is 1493 metres high. It is the highest mountain in Germany outside the Alps.

55759.q: Which waterfalls in the Black Forest are among the highest in Germany?
55759.e: At Triberg the Gutach drops a total of about 160 metres over several steps. The Rhine Falls carry more water but are much lower.
55759.m: The Triberg Waterfalls are a highlight of the Black Forest.

55760.q: What does the Black Forest Railway often have to go through on its way through the mountains?
55760.e: The Black Forest Railway runs from Offenburg to Konstanz. On its way it goes through almost 40 tunnels and many bends.
55760.m: The Black Forest Railway is a famous mountain railway.

55761.q: Which spa town with hot springs lies on the northern edge of the Black Forest?
55761.e: Even the Romans bathed in the warm springs of Baden-Baden. The town is still a well-known spa today.
55761.m: Baden-Baden is a spa town in the northern Black Forest.

55762.q: What does a national park such as the Black Forest National Park protect?
a: Nature with its plants and animals
55762.e: In the Black Forest National Park, founded in 2014, nature is allowed to develop as undisturbed as possible. It is the first national park in Baden-Württemberg.

55763.q: Which smoked speciality is named after the Black Forest?
55763.e: Black Forest ham is salted and cold-smoked over fir wood. Its name is protected and may only be used for ham from the region.
55763.m: Black Forest ham is smoked over fir wood.

55764.q: Why is Lake Constance important for millions of people?
55764.e: Drinking water for about four million people is taken from Lake Constance, mainly in southern Germany but also in Switzerland.
55764.m: Lake Constance is an important store of drinking water.

55765.q: Which island in Lake Constance is known for its flowers and gardens?
55765.e: The flower island of Mainau lies near Konstanz. Tulips, roses and dahlias bloom there, and there is a large butterfly house.
55765.m: Mainau is the flower island in Lake Constance.

55766.q: What is special about the national borders on the Obersee, the main part of Lake Constance?
a: They are not fixed by treaty
They run exactly through the middle of the lake
55766.e: Germany, Austria and Switzerland have never agreed on borders in the Obersee. In everyday life, rules for shipping and fishing set jointly by all three countries apply.
55766.m: There is no fixed border on the Obersee of Lake Constance.

55768.q: What is the name of the huge palace complex in central Vienna where the Habsburgs lived in winter?
55768.e: The Hofburg was the residence of the Habsburgs for over 600 years. Today it is, among other things, the official seat of the Austrian Federal President.
55768.m: The Hofburg was the Habsburgs' winter residence in Vienna.

55769.q: What is the name of the grand boulevard built around central Vienna in place of the old city wall?
55769.e: Emperor Franz Joseph had the city walls pulled down, and the Ringstrasse opened in 1865. The opera, parliament, city hall and university stand on it.
55769.m: Vienna's Ringstrasse replaced the old city wall.

55770.q: Which famous orchestra plays the New Year's Concert in Vienna every year on 1 January?
55770.e: The Vienna Philharmonic's New Year's Concert is broadcast to many countries. Mainly music by the Strauss family is played.
55770.m: The Vienna Philharmonic plays a famous concert on New Year's Day.

55771.q: Which Viennese tradition has been on Austria's list of intangible cultural heritage since 2011?
55771.e: In a Viennese coffee house you sit for a long time over a cup of coffee and a glass of water and read the newspaper. This tradition was recognised as intangible cultural heritage in 2011.
55771.m: Viennese coffee house culture is cultural heritage.

55772.q: Roughly how big is Austria compared with Switzerland?
55772.e: Austria has about 83,900 square kilometres, Switzerland about 41,300 square kilometres. So Austria is about twice as big.
55772.m: Austria is about twice as big as Switzerland.

55773.q: With which treaty did Austria regain its full independence on 15 May 1955?
a: Final Act of the Congress of Vienna
55773.e: After the Second World War, Austria was occupied by four victorious powers for ten years. With the State Treaty, the troops withdrew.
55773.m: The State Treaty of 1955 made Austria free again.

55774.q: In which country is the mountain village of Heiligenblut at the foot of the Grossglockner?
55774.e: Heiligenblut is in Carinthia in Austria. The pilgrimage church with the Grossglockner in the background is a popular photo subject.
55774.m: Heiligenblut is the mountain village below the Grossglockner.

55775.q: What is the viewpoint overlooking the Grossglockner that is named after an Austrian emperor called?
55775.e: The Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe lies at the end of a side road of the High Alpine Road. Emperor Franz Joseph visited the place in 1856.
55775.m: You can see the Grossglockner from the Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe.

55776.q: When is the Grossglockner High Alpine Road usually closed?
55776.e: The road climbs to about 2500 m. Because of snow and the risk of avalanches, it is closed from about November to early May.
55776.m: The Glockner road is closed in winter.

55777.q: What is the slightly lower secondary peak right next to the Grossglockner called?
55777.e: The Kleinglockner is about 3770 metres high and only about 80 metres from the main summit. A narrow notch lies between them.
55777.m: The Kleinglockner stands next to the Grossglockner.

55779.q: What is the Mirabell Garden in Salzburg?
a: A baroque garden with statues and flower beds
55779.e: The Mirabell Garden belongs to Mirabell Palace. From there you have a lovely view of the old town and the fortress.
55779.m: The Mirabell Garden is a famous baroque garden in Salzburg.

55780.q: What is Hellbrunn Palace near Salzburg especially known for?
55780.e: In the park of Hellbrunn Palace there are hidden fountains that surprise visitors by spraying them with water. The trick fountains have been working for over 400 years.
55780.m: Hellbrunn Palace is famous for its trick fountains.

55781.q: How did the rulers of Salzburg become rich in the past?
55781.e: The prince-archbishops ruled Salzburg for centuries. With the money from the salt trade they built magnificent churches and palaces.
55781.m: Salzburg became rich through the salt trade.

55782.q: Which village in the Salzkammergut is world-famous for its lakeside houses and its ancient salt mine?
55782.e: Hallstatt lies on Lake Hallstatt. Salt has been mined there for thousands of years, and the village is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
55782.m: Hallstatt is the most famous village in the Salzkammergut.

55783.q: In which country is the Salzkammergut?
55783.e: The Salzkammergut is in Austria, spread across Upper Austria, Salzburg and Styria.

55784.q: Which mountain range forms the border between Spain and France?
55784.e: The Pyrenees stretch from the Atlantic to the Mediterranean. The small country of Andorra also lies in them.
55784.m: The Pyrenees separate Spain from France.

55785.q: What form of state does Spain have?
55785.e: Spain has a king as head of state, but it is governed by an elected government and parliament.
55785.m: Spain is a parliamentary monarchy with a king.

55786.q: Which of these languages is an official language alongside Spanish in parts of Spain?
55786.e: In Catalonia, the Balearic Islands and Valencia, Catalan (or Valencian) is an official language. Other regional languages are Basque and Galician.
55786.m: Besides Spanish, people in Spain also speak Catalan, Basque and Galician.

55787.q: Into how many autonomous communities is Spain divided?
55787.e: Spain is made up of 17 autonomous communities, a bit like Switzerland with its 26 cantons.

55788.q: What is the name of the famous art museum in Madrid with works by Velázquez and Goya?
55788.e: The Prado opened in 1819 and is one of the most important art museums in the world.
55788.m: The Prado in Madrid is one of the most important art museums in the world.

55789.q: Which famous football club comes from Madrid?
55789.e: Real Madrid plays at the Santiago Bernabéu stadium. The club has won the Champions League more often than any other.
55789.m: Real Madrid is a football club from Madrid.

55790.q: Where in Spain is the capital Madrid?
a: In the far north by the sea
55790.e: Madrid lies almost exactly in the middle of Spain on a high plateau. It has been the seat of the royal court since 1561.
55790.m: Madrid is in the middle of Spain.

55791.q: At roughly what height above sea level is Madrid?
55791.e: Madrid lies on the Meseta plateau at about 650 m. That makes it one of the highest capitals in Europe, a little higher than Lausanne.
55791.m: Madrid is one of the highest capitals in Europe.

55793.q: Which park in Barcelona with colourful mosaics was designed by the architect Antoni Gaudí?
55793.e: Park Güell was created at the beginning of the 20th century and is famous for its lizard and the bench made of coloured pieces of broken tiles.
55793.m: Park Güell is a work by Gaudí.

55794.q: Which city is the capital of Andalusia?
55794.e: Seville lies on the Guadalquivir and is the largest city in Andalusia.
55794.m: Seville is the capital of Andalusia.

55795.q: In which city is the Moorish palace and fortress, the Alhambra?
55795.e: The Alhambra was built by Moorish rulers and has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1984.

55796.q: Which river is the most important river in Andalusia?
55796.e: The Guadalquivir flows through Córdoba and Seville and into the Atlantic. Ships can sail up it as far as Seville.
55796.m: The Guadalquivir is the main river of Andalusia.

55797.q: Which style of music and dance comes from Andalusia?
55797.e: Flamenco combines singing, guitar and dance and has been part of UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage since 2010.

55798.q: In which city is the Mezquita, a former mosque that is now a cathedral?
55798.e: The Mosque-Cathedral of Córdoba is famous for its forest of columns with red and white arches.

55799.q: Which product is made in very large quantities in Andalusia?
55799.e: Huge olive groves grow in Andalusia, especially in the province of Jaén. Spain is the largest producer of olive oil in the world.
55799.m: Andalusia is a stronghold of olive oil.

A coastal mountain range in Portugal
A group of islands in the Atlantic
A river delta on the Mediterranean
55800.e: The Meseta is the large plateau in the centre of the Iberian Peninsula and covers a large part of Spain.
55800.m: The Meseta is the plateau at the heart of Spain.

55801.q: At roughly what height does most of the Meseta lie?
55801.e: The Meseta mostly lies at 600 to 800 m, a little higher than the Swiss Plateau.
55801.m: The Meseta is higher than the Swiss Plateau.

55802.q: Which capital city lies in the middle of the Meseta?
55802.e: Madrid lies on the Meseta, the large plateau in the interior of Spain, at about 650 metres.

55803.q: What is the climate like on the Meseta?
a: Continental with hot summers and cold winters
55803.e: Because mountains keep out the sea air, it is very hot and dry in summer and cold in winter.
55803.m: On the Meseta the summers are hot and the winters cold.

55804.q: Which area on the southern Meseta is known for its windmills and the fictional character Don Quixote?
55804.e: In Miguel de Cervantes' novel, Don Quixote fights windmills that he thinks are giants. They stand in La Mancha.
55804.m: The windmills of La Mancha are famous from Don Quixote.

55805.q: What is traditionally grown most on the wide fields of the Meseta?
55805.e: On the dry plateau people have long grown mainly wheat and barley; there is also wine and sheep farming.
55805.m: The Meseta is one of Spain's breadbaskets.

55806.q: In which region of Spain are the Sierra Nevada mountains?
55806.e: The Sierra Nevada lies in the south-east of Andalusia, right next to Granada.
55806.m: The Sierra Nevada is in Andalusia.

55807.q: What often lies on the peaks of the Sierra Nevada in Spain until early summer?
55807.e: The Sierra Nevada is over 3400 metres high. Its name means snowy mountain range.
55807.m: Snow lies for a long time in the Sierra Nevada.

55808.q: What does the name “Sierra Nevada” mean in English?
55808.e: “Sierra” means mountain range and “nevada” means snowy. Snow often lies on the peaks until early summer.
55808.m: Sierra Nevada means snowy mountain range.

55809.q: Which big sporting event took place in the Sierra Nevada in 1996?
55809.e: The 1996 Alpine Ski World Championships were held in the Sierra Nevada ski area, the southernmost big ski area in Europe.
55809.m: You can ski in the Sierra Nevada in southern Spain.

55810.q: Which city lies right at the foot of the Sierra Nevada?
55810.e: From Granada you can see the often snowy peaks of the Sierra Nevada behind the Alhambra.
55810.m: Granada lies at the foot of the Sierra Nevada.

55811.q: What is special about the Ebro compared with Spain's other rivers?
a: It is the longest river that runs entirely in Spain
It is the only river that flows north
55811.e: The Ebro is about 910 km long. On the Iberian Peninsula only the Tagus is longer, and it also flows through Portugal.
55811.m: The Ebro is the longest river that flows only through Spain.

55812.q: What kind of landscape is found at the mouth of the Ebro?
a: A river delta with rice fields
55812.e: In the Ebro Delta the river deposits a lot of mud. There are rice fields, lagoons and many water birds.
55812.m: There is a large delta at the mouth of the Ebro.

55813.q: Which name for the whole peninsula probably comes from the ancient name of the Ebro?
55813.e: The Greeks and Romans called the river “Iberus”. The name Iberian Peninsula comes from this.
55813.m: The Iberian Peninsula is named after the Ebro.

55814.q: Who built the great stone bridge of Alcántara over the Tagus almost 2000 years ago?
55814.e: The Roman bridge of Alcántara was built around AD 104 to 106 under Emperor Trajan and still stands today.
55814.m: A Roman bridge crosses the Tagus at Alcántara.

55815.q: Which famous bridge in San Francisco does the red suspension bridge over the Tagus in Lisbon look like?
55815.e: The Ponte 25 de Abril in Lisbon opened in 1966. With its red colour it looks very similar to the Golden Gate Bridge.
55815.m: The Ponte 25 de Abril spans the Tagus in Lisbon.

55816.q: Through which two countries does the Tagus flow?
55816.e: The Tagus rises in eastern Spain, flows west and reaches the sea in Portugal.
55816.m: The Tagus flows through Spain and Portugal.

55817.q: Which is the largest of the Balearic Islands?
55817.e: At about 3600 km², Majorca is the largest Balearic island and one of the most popular holiday islands in Europe.
55817.m: Majorca is the largest Balearic island.

55818.q: What is the capital of the Balearic Islands?
55818.e: Palma is on Majorca and is known for its Gothic cathedral, La Seu, by the sea.
55818.m: Palma is the capital of the Balearic Islands.

55819.q: Which of these islands is one of the Balearic Islands?
55819.e: The Balearic Islands include Majorca, Minorca, Ibiza, Formentera and many small islands. Formentera is the smallest of the inhabited main islands.
55819.m: Formentera is the smallest of the four big Balearic islands.

55820.q: Which country do the Balearic Islands belong to?
55820.e: Majorca, Minorca, Ibiza and Formentera belong to Spain. The Serra de Tramuntana mountains are on Majorca.
55820.m: The Balearic Islands belong to Spain.

55821.q: In which ocean are the Canary Islands?
55821.e: The Canaries lie in the Atlantic off the coast of Africa, about 100 km west of Morocco.
55821.m: The Canary Islands lie in the Atlantic off Africa.

55822.q: On which Canary Island did a volcano erupt in 2021 and destroy many houses?
55822.e: The eruption in the Cumbre Vieja area lasted about three months. Lava flows destroyed over a thousand buildings.
55822.m: A volcano erupted on La Palma in 2021.

55823.q: On which island is the volcano Teide?
55823.e: Teide forms the centre of the island of Tenerife and can be seen from almost everywhere on the island.

a: Largest active volcano in the world
55824.e: Teide is higher than any mountain on the Spanish mainland, even higher than Mulhacén in the Sierra Nevada.
55824.m: Teide is the highest mountain in Spain.

55825.e: Teide is a volcano and, at about 3700 metres, the highest mountain in Spain. It rises inside a huge collapsed crater.

55826.q: Which group of islands does Tenerife belong to?
55826.e: Tenerife is the largest of the Canary Islands in the Atlantic off Africa. The islands belong to Spain.
55826.m: Tenerife is one of the Canary Islands.

55827.q: Which country is Portugal's only neighbour?
55827.e: Portugal lies in the west of the Iberian Peninsula and has only Spain as a neighbour; otherwise it borders the Atlantic.
55827.m: Portugal has only one neighbouring country: Spain.

55828.q: In which country is the westernmost point of mainland Europe?
55828.e: Cabo da Roca is near Lisbon in Portugal. Beyond it the open Atlantic begins.
55828.m: The westernmost point of mainland Europe is in Portugal.

55829.q: Which Portuguese seafarer found the sea route to India in 1498?
55829.e: Vasco da Gama sailed round the Cape of Good Hope to India. This began Portugal's trade with Asia.
55829.m: Vasco da Gama found the sea route to India in 1498.

55830.q: What is the name of the 1974 revolution that made Portugal a democracy?
55830.e: On 25 April 1974 the military overthrew the dictatorship with almost no bloodshed. People put carnations into the barrels of the soldiers' guns.
55830.m: With the Carnation Revolution, Portugal became a democracy in 1974.

55832.q: Which building in the Belém district once protected the entrance to Lisbon's harbour?
55832.e: The Belém Tower stands on the bank of the Tagus and was built at the beginning of the 16th century. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
55832.m: The Torre de Belém guarded the entrance to Lisbon's harbour.

55833.q: Which sad, longing style of music is typical of Lisbon?
55833.e: Fado is usually sung by one voice with a Portuguese guitar. It has been UNESCO intangible cultural heritage since 2011.
55833.m: Fado is the typical music of Lisbon.

55834.q: In which country does the Douro rise?
55834.e: The river rises in northern Spain, where it is called the Duero, and then flows through Portugal into the Atlantic.
55834.m: The Douro rises in Spain, where it is called the Duero.

55835.q: Which drink is made from the grapes of the Douro Valley?
55835.e: The grapes grow on steep terraces in the upper Douro Valley. Port used to be taken downriver to Porto by boat.
55835.m: Port wine comes from the Douro Valley.

55836.q: Which Portuguese city lies at the mouth of the Douro?
55836.e: Porto lies on the Douro just before the Atlantic. Port wine is named after the city.
55836.m: Porto lies at the mouth of the Douro.

55837.q: Where does Porto rank among Portugal's largest cities?
55837.e: Porto is the second largest city after Lisbon and the economic centre of northern Portugal.
55837.m: Porto is the second largest city in Portugal.

55838.q: What does the famous iron bridge Ponte Dom Luís I in Porto connect?
a: The two banks of the Douro
55838.e: The two-level bridge opened in 1886 and crosses the River Douro. The metro runs on top, cars below.
55838.m: The Ponte Dom Luís I crosses the Douro in Porto.

55839.q: What are the many cellars on the bank opposite Porto famous for?
55839.e: In Vila Nova de Gaia on the south bank of the Douro, port wine matures in large barrels. It is named after the city of Porto.
55839.m: The port wine cellars are opposite Porto.

55840.q: Which country's name comes from the old name of the area around Porto?
55840.e: The Romans called the settlement at the mouth of the Douro “Portus Cale”. The name Portugal developed from this.
55840.m: Portugal gets its name from the area around Porto.

55841.q: Where is Porto's old town with its colourful houses?
a: On the bank of the River Douro
On an island in the Atlantic
In the middle of a desert
55841.e: The old Ribeira district lies right on the Douro. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1996.
55841.m: Porto's old town lies on the Douro.

55842.q: Which town is the main town of the Algarve, with an international airport?
55842.e: Faro is the administrative centre of the region. Millions of holidaymakers arrive through its airport every year.
55842.m: Faro is the main town of the Algarve.

55843.q: Which sea is the coast of the Algarve in Portugal on?
55843.e: The Algarve is in the far south of Portugal. Its coast borders the Atlantic Ocean, not far from the Strait of Gibraltar.
55843.m: The Algarve lies on the Atlantic.

55844.q: Which branch of the economy is most important in the Algarve today?
55844.e: Sun, beaches and golf courses attract many visitors. Tourism is the region's biggest source of income.
55844.m: People in the Algarve live mainly from tourism.

55845.q: Which prince promoted the Portuguese voyages of discovery from Sagres in the Algarve?
55845.e: In the 15th century Henry the Navigator had voyages organised along the coast of Africa.
55845.m: Henry the Navigator promoted Portugal's voyages of discovery.

55846.q: Which country do the Azores belong to?
55846.e: The Azores are nine islands in the middle of the Atlantic. They belong to Portugal.

55847.q: Which mountain in the Azores is the highest in Portugal?
55847.e: The volcano Pico on the island of the same name is 2351 m high, making it the highest mountain in Portugal.
55847.m: Pico in the Azores is the highest mountain in Portugal.

55848.q: In which ocean are the Azores?
55848.e: The Azores lie in the middle of the Atlantic, about 1400 km west of Portugal. The largest island is called São Miguel.
55848.m: The Azores lie in the Atlantic.

55849.q: Which group of islands gives its name to a well-known high-pressure area that affects our weather?
55849.e: The Azores High often sits over the Atlantic near the Azores. When it spreads to central Europe, it brings fine summer weather to Switzerland too.
55849.m: The Azores High often brings us fine weather.

55850.q: Which country does the island of Madeira belong to?
55850.e: Madeira lies in the Atlantic off Africa and belongs to Portugal. The island's capital is Funchal.

55851.q: What are the narrow irrigation channels on Madeira called, along which you can walk?
55851.e: The levadas carry water from the rainy north to the drier south, similar to the bisses in Valais.
55851.m: On Madeira you walk along the levadas.

55852.e: Madeira lies in the Atlantic, about 700 kilometres off the coast of Africa. There is an ancient laurel forest on the island.

55853.q: Which country does Gibraltar belong to?
55853.e: Gibraltar is a British Overseas Territory at the southern tip of Spain. Spain still claims it today.
55853.m: Gibraltar is a British Overseas Territory.

55854.q: Roughly how wide is the Strait of Gibraltar at its narrowest point?
55854.e: At the narrowest point only about 14 km separate Europe from Africa; in clear weather you can see Morocco.
55854.m: At Gibraltar, Europe and Africa are only about 14 km apart.

55857.q: What is unusual about Gibraltar's airport?
55857.e: The main road to the Spanish border used to cross the runway. Since 2023 cars have used a tunnel, but pedestrians may still cross the runway when no plane is taking off or landing.
55857.m: In Gibraltar pedestrians walk across the runway.

55858.q: Who is King of Spain (as of 2026)?
55858.e: Felipe VI has been King of Spain since 2014. He succeeded his father Juan Carlos I, who abdicated.
55858.m: Felipe VI has been King of Spain since 2014.

55859.q: Which northern Spanish city is known for the Guggenheim Museum with its shiny titanium façade?
55859.e: The Guggenheim Museum in Bilbao opened in 1997 and was designed by the architect Frank Gehry.
55859.m: The Guggenheim Museum is in Bilbao in the Basque Country.

55860.q: What is the name of the great royal palace in Madrid?
55860.e: The Palacio Real is the official residence of the Spanish royal family, but it is only used for state occasions.
55860.m: The Palacio Real is the royal palace of Madrid.

55861.q: What is the name of the rectangular main square with arcades in Madrid's old town?
55861.e: The Plaza Mayor was built in the 17th century. Markets, festivals and bullfights used to take place here.
55861.m: The Plaza Mayor is Madrid's historic main square.

55862.q: Which famous church by Antoni Gaudí in Barcelona has been under construction for over 140 years?
55862.e: Work on the Sagrada Família began in 1882 and is still not quite finished. Notre-Dame is in Paris, St Peter's in Rome and Cologne Cathedral in Germany.
55862.m: The Sagrada Família is Gaudí's most famous church.

55864.q: Through which region, known for its red wine, does the Ebro flow?
55864.e: The Ebro flows through La Rioja and its capital Logroño. The region is the best-known wine region in Spain.
55864.m: The Ebro flows through the La Rioja wine region.

55866.q: Why is the Ebro Delta protected as a nature park?
55866.e: Hundreds of thousands of birds, including flamingos, nest and rest in the lagoons and marshes of the delta.
55866.m: The Ebro Delta is an important home for water birds.

55867.q: Roughly how long is the Tagus?
55867.e: The Tagus is about 1000 km long, and the larger part of it is in Spain.
55867.m: The Tagus is about 1000 km long.

55868.q: At which capital city does the Tagus flow into the Atlantic?
55868.e: The Tagus flows west from Spain and reaches the Atlantic at Lisbon.
55868.m: The Tagus reaches the sea at Lisbon.

55869.q: In which direction does the Tagus flow through Spain and Portugal?
55869.e: The Tagus rises in the east of Spain and flows west to the Atlantic at Lisbon.
55869.m: The Tagus flows west to the Atlantic.

55870.q: In which sea are the Balearic Islands?
55870.e: The Balearic Islands lie in the western Mediterranean off the east coast of Spain.
55870.m: The Balearic Islands lie in the Mediterranean.

55871.q: Why do most visitors travel to Balearic islands such as Majorca or Ibiza?
a: For beach holidays by the sea
55871.e: The Balearic Islands have warm summers, beaches and clear water. Tourism is the most important part of the economy there.
55871.m: The Balearic Islands are popular beach islands.

55873.q: On which Canary Island is Teide, the highest mountain in Spain?
55873.e: Teide on Tenerife is a volcano about 3700 metres high. It is the highest mountain in Spain.
55873.m: Teide on Tenerife is Spain's highest mountain.

55874.q: Which continent are the Canary Islands closest to?
55874.e: The Canaries lie in the Atlantic only about 100 kilometres off the coast of Africa. Politically they belong to Spain.
55874.m: The Canaries lie close to Africa.

55875.q: Which vehicles travel through the steep lanes of Lisbon's old town?
55875.e: Lisbon's yellow trams even run through narrow, steep lanes, for example in the old Alfama district.
55875.m: Lisbon is known for its yellow trams.

55876.q: How were the port wine barrels brought from the Douro Valley to Porto in the past?
a: By wooden boats on the river
55876.e: Flat wooden boats called rabelos carried the barrels downriver to Porto. Today they mainly sail for tourists.
55876.m: Port wine used to travel by boat on the Douro.

55877.q: In which country is the holiday region of the Algarve?
55877.e: The Algarve is the southernmost region of Portugal. It is known for beaches, rocky coasts and lots of sunshine.

55878.q: In which part of Portugal is the Algarve?
a: On an island in the Atlantic
In the middle of the interior
55878.e: The Algarve is the southernmost strip of Portugal. To the north of it lies the Alentejo region.
55878.m: The Algarve is the south of Portugal.

55879.q: Which nickname does Madeira have because of its many plants and flowers?
55879.e: Because of the mild climate, flowers such as orchids and birds of paradise bloom on Madeira all year round.
55879.m: Madeira is also called the Island of Flowers.

55880.q: Which currency do you pay with in Gibraltar?
55880.e: Gibraltar has its own pound, which is fixed to the British pound. British pounds are also accepted.
55880.m: In Gibraltar you pay with the Gibraltar pound.

55881.q: Which Spanish city on the coast of Africa lies opposite Gibraltar?
55881.e: Ceuta is on the African side of the strait and belongs to Spain. Tangier belongs to Morocco.
55881.m: Ceuta is a Spanish city in Africa opposite Gibraltar.

55882.q: Which nickname has Rome had since ancient times?
55882.e: Rome is called “the Eternal City” because even the ancient Romans believed their city would last for ever.
55882.m: Rome has been called the Eternal City since ancient times.

55883.q: What is the name of the large ancient amphitheatre in Rome where gladiators fought?
55883.e: The Colosseum was built in the 1st century AD and had room for tens of thousands of spectators. It is Rome's landmark.
55883.m: Gladiators once fought in the Colosseum.

55884.q: On how many hills is ancient Rome said to have been founded?
55884.e: Rome is known as the “City of Seven Hills”, which include the Palatine and the Capitoline.
55884.m: Ancient Rome grew up on seven hills.

55885.q: According to legend, which twins founded Rome?
55885.e: According to legend, Romulus and Remus were fed by a she-wolf. Romulus is then said to have founded the city in 753 BC.
55885.m: Romulus and Remus are the legendary founders of Rome.

55886.q: In which mountains does the Tiber rise?
55886.e: The Tiber rises on Monte Fumaiolo in the Apennines and then flows south towards Rome.
55886.m: The Tiber comes from the Apennines.

55887.q: Roughly how long is the Tiber?
55887.e: The Tiber is about 405 km long, making it one of the longest rivers in Italy, and it flows from north to south through central Italy.
55887.m: The Tiber is roughly 400 kilometres long.

55888.q: Which mountain range runs through Italy from north to south like a backbone?
55888.e: The Apennines run through almost the whole Italian peninsula, from Liguria to Calabria. That is why they are called the backbone of Italy.
55888.m: The Apennines are the backbone of Italy.

55889.q: Through which country do the Apennine mountains run?
55889.e: The Apennines run for about 1200 km through Italy, from Liguria in the north to Calabria in the south.

55890.q: Which large predator still lives in small numbers in the forests of the Abruzzo in the Apennines?
55890.e: A small subspecies of brown bear, the Marsican brown bear, lives in the Abruzzo National Park. There are only a few dozen left.
55890.m: Rare brown bears still live in the Apennines.

55891.q: Why are there earthquakes again and again in the Apennines?
a: Two tectonic plates push against each other
55891.e: Under Italy the African and Eurasian Plates meet. The stress is released as earthquakes, for example in L'Aquila in 2009.
55891.m: Italy has earthquakes because tectonic plates move there.

55892.q: Roughly how long are the Apennines?
55892.e: The Apennines stretch for about 1200 km from Liguria to Calabria.
55892.m: The Apennines are over a thousand kilometres long.

55893.q: Which is the longest river in Italy?
55893.e: The Po is about 650 km long, making it the longest river in Italy.
55893.m: The Po is the longest river in Italy.

55894.q: What is the name of the largest lowland plain in Italy?
55894.e: The Po Valley lies in northern Italy between the Alps and the Apennines. It is the largest plain in the country.
55894.m: The largest plain in Italy is the Po Valley.

55895.q: Into which sea does the Po flow?
55895.e: The Po flows east and reaches the Adriatic south of Venice through a large delta.
55895.m: The Po flows into the Adriatic.

55896.q: Which cereal is grown a lot in the Po Valley and used for risotto?
55896.e: There are huge rice fields around Vercelli, Novara and Pavia. Italy is the largest rice producer in Europe.
55896.m: A lot of rice for risotto grows in the Po Valley.

55897.q: Which river from Switzerland flows into the Po?
55897.e: The River Ticino rises in the canton of Ticino, flows through Lake Maggiore and joins the Po near Pavia.
55897.m: The River Ticino flows from Switzerland into the Po.

55898.q: Which big city lies right on the Po?
55898.e: Turin, the capital of Piedmont, lies on the Po. The river is already quite wide there.
55898.m: Turin lies on the banks of the Po.

55899.q: What weather is typical in the Po Valley in autumn and winter?
55899.e: In the damp plain with little wind, thick fog often forms in autumn and winter, similar to the Swiss Plateau.
55899.m: In winter fog often lies over the Po Valley.

55900.q: What is the capital of Tuscany?
55900.e: Florence is the capital and largest city of the region of Tuscany.
55900.m: The capital of Tuscany is Florence.

55901.q: Which famous leaning building stands in Tuscany?
55901.e: The bell tower of Pisa Cathedral began to lean while it was still being built, because the ground underneath is soft.
55901.m: The leaning tower is in Pisa.

55902.q: Which trees, like slim dark columns, mark many landscapes in Tuscany?
55902.e: Tall cypresses line roads and hills in Tuscany. They are typical of the Tuscan landscape.
55902.m: Slim cypresses are typical of Tuscany.

55903.q: What is the famous horse race on the main square of Siena called?
55903.e: In the Palio of Siena, the city districts race against each other twice every summer on the Piazza del Campo.
55903.m: The Palio horse race takes place in Siena.

55904.q: Which island off Tuscany was Napoleon's place of exile in 1814?
55904.e: Napoleon was exiled to Elba in 1814, but escaped back to France as early as 1815.
55904.m: Napoleon lived in exile on Elba in 1814.

55905.q: What is the name of the well-known wine region between Florence and Siena?
55905.e: Chianti lies in the hills between Florence and Siena and is known for its red wine.
55905.m: Chianti lies between Florence and Siena.
