a: All heights in Switzerland are measured from it
It marks the centre of Switzerland
It is the oldest boundary stone
It shows the highest water level
57176.e: On the erratic boulder Pierre du Niton there is a reference point for height. The heights of all places and mountains in Switzerland were worked out from it.
57176.m: All Swiss height measurements refer to an erratic boulder in Geneva.

57177.q: Why are many erratic boulders protected today?
a: They are important evidence of the ice age
57177.e: Erratic boulders show how far the glaciers reached during the ice age. Because many were broken up in the past, the remaining ones are protected today.
57177.m: Erratic boulders are protected evidence of the ice age.

57178.q: When did huge glaciers bring the erratic boulders to the Central Plateau?
57178.e: In the ice age, the Alpine glaciers reached far into the Central Plateau. When they melted, the boulders they had carried were left behind.
57178.m: Erratic boulders were carried by glaciers during the ice age.

57179.q: Why were many erratic boulders on the Central Plateau destroyed in the past?
a: They were used as building stone
They were thought to be poisonous
57179.e: Erratic boulders were a handy raw material for walls, steps and fountains. That is why many were broken up before they were protected.
57179.m: Many erratic boulders used to end up as building material.

57180.q: Which rock, not otherwise found there, are many erratic boulders on the Central Plateau made of?
57180.e: Granite comes from the Alps. If a granite boulder lies on the Central Plateau, a glacier brought it there. Nagelfluh and sandstone occur naturally on the Central Plateau too.
57180.m: Many erratic boulders on the Central Plateau are made of Alpine granite.

57181.q: What covered large parts of the Swiss Central Plateau during the last ice age?
57181.e: In the last ice age, huge glaciers flowed out of the Alps onto the Central Plateau. They shaped valleys, hills and lake basins.
57181.m: In the ice age, glacier ice lay on the Central Plateau.

57182.q: About how many years ago were the glaciers of the last ice age at their largest?
57182.e: The maximum of the last glaciation was about 24,000 years ago. At that time, ice covered large parts of the Central Plateau.
57182.m: About 24,000 years ago the Central Plateau was under ice.

57183.q: How did many large lakes on the Swiss Central Plateau, such as Lake Zurich, form?
57183.e: The ice-age glaciers deepened valleys and created basins. After the ice melted, they filled with water, often also dammed by moraines.
57183.m: The large lakes of the Central Plateau are a gift of the ice age.

57184.q: Which glacier of the last ice age reached from Valais as far as the Solothurn area?
57184.e: The ice-age Rhône Glacier flowed over the Lake Geneva area onto the Central Plateau. It reached as far as the area of Solothurn and Wangen an der Aare.
57184.m: In the ice age, the Rhône Glacier covered the western Central Plateau.

57185.q: About how many years ago did the last ice age end?
57185.e: When the last cold period ended, about 11,700 years ago, the Holocene began. We are still living in this warm period today.
57185.m: We have been living in a warm period for about 11,700 years.

57186.q: What is the cool period between about 1300 and 1850, when the glaciers grew again, called?
57186.e: In the Little Ice Age, summers were cooler and the Alpine glaciers advanced several times. Many villages in the Alps were threatened by growing glaciers at that time.
57186.m: The Little Ice Age made the glaciers grow until 1850.

a: A rock surface polished smooth by ice
A crack in the glacier ice
57187.e: Stones on the underside of the glacier grind the rock smooth and leave scratches. The scratches show the direction the ice flowed.
57187.m: Glacier polish is rock polished by the ice.

57188.q: Which wind usually brings rain from the Atlantic to the north side of the Alps?
57188.e: Switzerland lies in the westerly wind zone. West winds bring moist air from the Atlantic and so often bring rain to the north side of the Alps.
57188.m: The west wind often brings rain to northern Switzerland.

57189.q: Which region of Switzerland has the mildest climate and the most palm trees in gardens?
57189.e: Ticino lies on the south side of the Alps and is protected from cold north winds. The mild winters allow palms, camellias and fig trees.
57189.m: The climate on the south side of the Alps is especially mild.

57190.q: What is the warm, dry downslope wind called that occurs on the north side of the Alps when the wind is from the south?
57190.e: With a south föhn, the air drops its rain on the south side of the Alps. On the north side it sinks, warms up and becomes dry and warm.
57190.m: The föhn is a warm downslope wind from the Alps.

57191.q: What is the weather usually like on the south side of the Alps during a south föhn?
a: It is icy cold and dry
It is foggy with no rain
57191.e: The moist air piles up against the south side of the Alps and rises. As it does so it cools down, and a lot of rain or snow falls.
57191.m: With a south föhn it rains in the south and is warm in the north.

57192.q: Which region is one of the driest in Switzerland because it is surrounded by high mountains?
57192.e: The Rhône valley in Central Valais lies in the rain shadow of the Bernese and Valais Alps. That is why little rain falls there, and fields need watering.
57192.m: Central Valais lies in the rain shadow of the mountains.

57193.q: Which temperature, measured in Grono in the Mesolcina in 2003, was Switzerland’s heat record?
57193.e: On 11 August 2003, 41.5 degrees was measured in Grono in the canton of Grisons. That is Switzerland’s official heat record.

57194.q: In which place in the Neuchâtel Jura was Switzerland’s lowest temperature measured in 1987?
57194.e: On 12 January 1987, minus 41.8 degrees was measured in La Brévine. That is why the village is known as the “Siberia of Switzerland”.
57194.m: La Brévine is the Siberia of Switzerland.

57195.q: Why is it usually colder on the mountains than in the valley?
a: The air cools down the higher you go
The snow makes the air cold
There is more wind from the north there
57195.e: On average, the temperature drops by about 0.5 to 0.6 degrees for every 100 metres of height. That is why it is cooler higher up.
57195.m: The higher you climb, the colder it usually gets.

57196.q: Which direction does the bise blow from?
57196.e: The bise is a cold, dry wind from the north-east to east. It blows through the Central Plateau between the Jura and the Alps.
57196.m: The bise comes from the north-east.

57197.q: Where in Switzerland is the bise usually strongest?
57197.e: Between the Jura and the Alps, the Central Plateau gets narrower and narrower towards the south-west. So the bise speeds up as if in a funnel and is strongest on Lake Geneva.
57197.m: The bise blows hardest on Lake Geneva.

57198.q: What does the bise usually feel like in winter?
57198.e: The bise brings continental air from the north-east. In winter this air is cold and dry, so it feels even colder.
57198.m: The bise is a cold, dry wind.

57199.q: In which weather situation does the bise typically develop in Switzerland?
a: High pressure in the north and low pressure in the south
Low pressure in the north and high pressure in the south
57199.e: When there is a high over northern Europe and a low in the Mediterranean, air flows into Switzerland from the north-east. We call this flow the bise.
57199.m: The bise blows from a high in the north to a low in the south.

57200.q: What is the bise called when the sky is cloudy and grey?
57200.e: With the black bise the sky is overcast, often with high fog. With the ordinary bise, on the other hand, it is usually sunny.
57200.m: The black bise comes with a grey sky.

57201.q: What formed in Versoix on Lake Geneva in February 2012 because of strong bise and cold?
a: Thick layers of ice on cars and shores
57201.e: The bise whipped lake water onto the shores, trees and parked cars. In the extreme cold, it froze immediately into thick layers of ice.
57201.m: Bise and cold can cover everything in ice on Lake Geneva.

57202.q: Which mountain range, together with the Alps, forms the “funnel” that the bise blows through?
57202.e: The Central Plateau lies between the Jura and the Alps. The two mountain ranges guide the bise and make it stronger towards the south-west.
57202.m: The Jura and the Alps steer the bise through the Central Plateau.

57203.q: Which wind is the opposite of the bise in Switzerland and often brings rain?
57203.e: The bise comes cold and dry from the north-east. The west wind, on the other hand, brings moist air from the Atlantic and often rain.
57203.m: The west wind brings rain, the bise dry cold.

57204.q: What is a sea of fog?
a: A layer of fog seen from above
A lake that freezes in winter
A rain shower over the sea
57204.e: When a thick layer of fog or high fog lies in the valley, it looks like a sea from a mountain. The sun often shines above it.
57204.m: From a mountain, fog looks like a sea.

57205.q: In which seasons is there especially often a sea of fog on the Swiss Central Plateau?
57205.e: In long, cold nights the ground cools down a lot, and the air becomes damp and cold. In calm high-pressure weather, fog then forms easily.
57205.m: Seas of fog occur mainly in autumn and winter.

57206.q: What is the weather situation called when cold air lies below and warmer air above it?
57206.e: Normally it gets colder the higher you go. In an inversion it is the other way round, and fog stays trapped under the warm layer.
57206.m: In an inversion it is warmer above than below.

57207.q: Which weather situation favours a sea of fog on the Central Plateau?
a: a calm area of high pressure
a strong area of low pressure
57207.e: With high pressure it is calm and clear, so the air cools down a lot at night. The cold, damp air collects on the Central Plateau and forms fog.
57207.m: High pressure and calm bring fog to the Central Plateau.

57208.q: How high is the top of the sea of fog on the Central Plateau often?
57208.e: The top of the fog is often between about 800 and 1200 metres above sea level. Anyone who climbs mountains such as the Rigi or the Napf comes out into the sun.
57208.m: Above about a thousand metres the sun often shines above the fog.

57209.q: Why do many people escape to excursion mountains such as Pilatus on foggy days?
a: The sun shines above the fog
It is always warmer there than by the sea
57209.e: In an inversion, the fog lies only in the lower areas. On the mountains it is sunny and often even warmer than in the valley.
57209.m: Above the sea of fog it is often sunny.

57210.q: What usually breaks up a sea of fog?
a: Wind or a new weather front
57210.e: Wind mixes the air and ends the inversion. A weather front also brings new air and drives the fog away.
57210.m: Wind and changes in the weather drive away the sea of fog.

57211.q: What is the difference between high fog and ground fog?
a: High fog lies above the ground, ground fog reaches down to the ground
High fog only occurs in the mountains
Ground fog only occurs in summer
57211.e: With high fog, the grey layer hangs a few hundred metres up, and you can see far below it. Ground fog lies right on the ground and makes it very hard to see.
57211.m: High fog floats, ground fog lies on the ground.

57212.q: What does the snow line mean?
a: The height above which snow stays lying
The height above which trees grow
The border between rain and sun
57212.e: Above the snow line there is snow; below it the ground is free of snow. Its height changes with the season and the weather.
57212.m: Above the snow line, snow stays lying.

57213.q: What is the climatic snow line?
a: The height above which snow no longer melts even in summer
The height where it first snows in winter
The line above which avalanches start
The height at which ski lifts are built
57213.e: Above the climatic snow line, more snow falls each year than melts. Only there can glaciers form.
57213.m: Glacier ice forms above the climatic snow line.

57214.q: What is the line on a glacier called where gain and melting balance each other?
57214.e: At the equilibrium line, exactly as much melts in a year as is added in snow. It roughly matches the snow line at the end of summer.
57214.m: The equilibrium line separates the accumulation zone and the ablation zone.

57215.q: What do you call the upper part of a glacier, where more snow falls than melts?
57215.e: In the accumulation zone, snow builds up and turns into firn and later into ice. The ice then flows down into the ablation zone.
57215.m: The glacier grows in the accumulation zone.

57216.q: What do you call snow that has lasted through at least one summer and is already grainy?
57216.e: Firn is snow that is several years old and packed down. When it is pressed together further, it turns into glacier ice.
57216.m: Snow becomes firn, and firn becomes glacier ice.

57217.q: Why is the snow line higher in the inner Alps, for example in Valais, than at the northern edge of the Alps?
a: Less rain and snow fall there and it is sunnier
57217.e: The inner Alpine valleys are drier and sunnier than the rainy edge of the Alps. Because less snow falls, you have to climb higher before it stays lying.
57217.m: In dry areas the snow line is higher.

57218.q: What happens to the snow line when the climate gets warmer?
57218.e: At higher temperatures, snow melts even at greater heights. That is why the snow line rises, and the glaciers do not get enough new snow.
57218.m: A warmer climate pushes the snow line upwards.

57219.q: What does the weather forecast mean by the snowfall line?
a: The height above which rain and snow fall as snow
The height above which nothing falls
The height of the sea of fog
57219.e: Below the snowfall line it rains; above it, snow falls. It is given in metres above sea level.
57219.m: Above the snowfall line, snow falls instead of rain.

a: The national weather and climate service
57220.e: MeteoSwiss is the Federal Office of Meteorology and Climatology. It makes weather forecasts, issues warnings and monitors the climate.
57220.m: MeteoSwiss is the Confederation’s official weather service.

57221.q: Where does MeteoSwiss have its headquarters?
57221.e: The headquarters of MeteoSwiss is at Zurich Airport. Other sites are in Geneva, Payerne and Locarno.
57221.m: MeteoSwiss works mainly at Zurich Airport.

57222.q: How many danger levels do MeteoSwiss weather warnings have?
57222.e: The warnings range from level 1 (no or low danger) to level 5 (very high danger). The colours go from green to dark red.
57222.m: Weather warnings have five danger levels.

57223.q: What does MeteoSwiss use weather radars for?
57223.e: Weather radars send out signals that bounce back off raindrops and snowflakes. This shows where it is raining or snowing right now.
57223.m: Weather radars show where it is raining or snowing.

57224.q: What do the weather balloons that MeteoSwiss sends up measure?
a: Temperature, humidity and wind high up
The number of fish in the lakes
The number of aeroplanes in the sky
57224.e: A radiosonde hangs from the balloons. As it rises to over 30 kilometres, it measures temperature, humidity and wind and radios the values back to Earth.
57224.m: Weather balloons measure the weather high up.

57225.q: What does MeteoSwiss do when a strong storm is on the way?
57225.e: MeteoSwiss issues severe weather warnings, for example by app, radio and television. That way people can protect themselves.

57226.q: Which instrument does a weather station use to measure air pressure?
57226.e: A barometer measures air pressure. When it falls, bad weather often follows. A thermometer measures temperature.
57226.m: Air pressure is measured with a barometer.

57227.q: Which international organisation, where MeteoSwiss represents Switzerland, has its headquarters in Geneva?
57227.e: The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) is a UN organisation based in Geneva. MeteoSwiss is Switzerland’s official representative there.
57227.m: The World Meteorological Organization is based in Geneva.

57228.q: What is the lowest altitude zone in Switzerland called, where growing wine and fruit is typical?
57228.e: The colline zone is the hill zone at low altitudes. It is warm enough there for vines, fruit and crops.
57228.m: Vines and fruit grow in the colline zone.

57229.q: Which altitude zone comes directly above the colline zone in the Alps?
57229.e: Above the hill zone, the montane zone begins. It is the mountain forest zone with beech, fir and spruce forests.
57229.m: The montane zone comes above the hill zone.

57230.q: Which broadleaved tree is typical of forests in the montane zone on the north side of the Alps?
57230.e: Beech and fir forests often grow in the montane zone. The Swiss stone pine grows higher up, the sweet chestnut mainly on the south side of the Alps.
57230.m: The beech is a typical tree of the mountain forest zone.

57231.q: Which conifers are typical of the subalpine zone near the tree line?
57231.e: Larch and Swiss stone pine cope very well with cold and short summers. They often form the highest forest in the subalpine zone.
57231.m: Larches and Swiss stone pines grow up to the tree line.

57232.q: At roughly what height is the tree line in the Swiss Alps?
57232.e: The tree line is lower at the northern edge of the Alps and higher in the drier inner Alps. In the Central Alps it can reach over 2200 metres.
57232.m: Above about 2000 metres the forest ends in the Alps.

57233.q: What typically grows in the alpine zone above the tree line?
a: Alpine pastures with grasses and dwarf shrubs
57233.e: Above the tree line it is too cold for trees. There are grassland, alpine flowers and low shrubs such as the alpenrose.
57233.m: Grass and alpine flowers grow in the alpine zone.

57234.q: What is the highest altitude zone, with rock, snow and ice, called?
57234.e: The nival zone lies above the snow line. Plants grow there only here and there in cracks in the rock, for example the glacier buttercup.
57234.m: The nival zone is the zone of snow and ice.

57235.q: Why are the altitude zones on the south side of the Alps usually a little higher than on the north side?
a: Because there is more bise there
Because the mountains are lower there
Because there is more fog there
57235.e: On the sunny, mild south side of the Alps, plants can grow higher up. That is why the limits of the zones move upwards.
57235.m: Warmth makes the altitude zones move upwards.

57236.q: Where are cows traditionally driven in summer to graze in the alpine and subalpine zones?
57236.e: At the drive up to the alp in early summer, farmers move up with their animals. In autumn they return to the valley in the drive down from the alp.
57236.m: In summer the cows graze on the alp.

57237.q: What is often left behind when a glacier shrinks back out of a valley?
a: A glacier forefield with rubble and new lakes
57237.e: After the retreat, rubble, moraines and often new glacier lakes are uncovered. Plants settle on this forefield only slowly.
57237.m: Retreating glaciers leave a glacier forefield behind.

57238.q: Which place on the south side of the Alps is one of the sunniest in Switzerland?
57238.e: Locarno on Lake Maggiore has especially many hours of sunshine each year. Its position south of the Alps shields it from many clouds from the north.
57238.m: Locarno is one of the sunniest places in Switzerland.

57239.q: Roughly what area did the Great Aletsch Glacier cover in 2017?
57239.e: In 2017 the glacier covered about 78.5 square kilometres. Around 1850 it was still about 105 square kilometres.
57239.m: The Aletsch Glacier has got smaller but is still huge.

a: A hole in the rock hollowed out by meltwater
A cooking pot used by mountain farmers
A glacier lake on the ice
57240.e: Under the glacier, meltwater swirled round in circles with stones. These stones ground round, deep holes into the rock.
57240.m: Glacier potholes were drilled by swirling meltwater.

57241.q: What do you call a hollow that forms when a block of ice left in the ground melts?
57241.e: After the ice age, blocks of ice were left trapped in moraine rubble. When they melted, the ground sank, and hollows formed, often with small lakes or bogs.
57241.m: A kettle hole is the hollow left by a melted block of ice.

57242.q: What do granite boulders from Valais lying on the slopes of the Jura prove?
a: The Rhône Glacier reached as far as the Jura
The Jura used to be a volcano
The boulders come from the Jura itself
57242.e: Granite does not occur in the Jura, but it does in the Valais Alps. Only the ice-age Rhône Glacier could have carried the boulders so far.
57242.m: Valais boulders on the Jura show how big the Rhône Glacier was.

57243.q: From which summit above Fiesch is there a famous view of the Aletsch Glacier?
57243.e: The Eggishorn lies in the Goms above Fiesch and can be reached by cable car. From there you can see the glacier for many kilometres.
57243.m: From the Eggishorn you can look out over the Aletsch Glacier.

57244.q: At most, how fast does the ice of the Aletsch Glacier flow near Konkordiaplatz?
a: up to about 180 metres per year
up to about 18 metres per day
up to about 1.8 metres per year
up to about 18 kilometres per year
57244.e: Glacier ice moves slowly down the valley. Near Konkordiaplatz, the Aletsch Glacier reaches up to about 180 metres per year.
57244.m: Glacier ice flows slowly but steadily down the valley.

57245.q: What is Bern officially called, because the Federal Constitution does not name a capital?
57245.e: According to the Constitution, Switzerland has no capital. Bern is the seat of the Federal Council and Parliament and is therefore called the federal city.
57245.m: Bern is the federal city of Switzerland.

57246.q: In which year was Bern chosen as the seat of the federal authorities?
57246.e: After the federal state was founded in 1848, the Federal Assembly chose Bern as the seat of the federal authorities in the same year.
57246.m: The Federal Council and Parliament have met in Bern since 1848.

57247.q: Which river flows around Bern’s old town in a tight loop?
57247.e: Bern’s old town lies on a rocky ridge around which the Aare forms a large loop.
57247.m: The Aare flows around the old town of Bern.

57248.q: Which building in Bern houses Parliament and the Federal Council?
57248.e: The National Council and the Council of States meet in the Federal Palace, and the Federal Council also has its rooms there.
57248.m: The Federal Palace is the heart of Swiss politics in Bern.

57249.q: Which ducal family founded Bern in 1191?
57249.e: Duke Berthold V of Zähringen founded the city of Bern in 1191.
57249.m: Bern was founded by the Zähringens.

57251.q: What is the snowman called whose head explodes at Zurich’s Sechseläuten festival?
57251.e: At the Sechseläuten, the Böögg is burnt on a pile of wood. The faster its head explodes, the nicer the summer is supposed to be.
57251.m: At the Sechseläuten, the people of Zurich burn the Böögg.

57252.q: In which year was ETH Zurich founded?
57252.e: The Swiss Federal Institute of Technology was founded in 1855 as the Polytechnikum and is one of the best-known universities in the world.

57253.q: Which river is the city of Basel on?
57253.e: The Rhine divides Basel into Grossbasel and Kleinbasel and makes a striking bend here, the Rhine Knee.
57253.m: Basel lies on the Rhine Knee.

57254.q: Why is the Rhine port of Basel important for Switzerland?
a: It is the way to the North Sea
It is only used for day trips
57254.e: Ships can travel along the Rhine from Basel all the way to Rotterdam on the North Sea. Oil, grain and containers are transported this way.
57254.m: Through Basel’s Rhine port, Switzerland is connected to the sea.

57255.q: Which industry shapes Basel especially strongly?
57255.e: Large chemical and pharmaceutical companies have their headquarters in Basel. They are important employers in the region.
57255.m: Basel is a centre of the pharmaceutical industry.

57256.q: In which country is the EuroAirport Basel-Mulhouse-Freiburg located?
57256.e: The EuroAirport lies on French soil near Saint-Louis, but it has its own Swiss customs sector.

57257.q: Which artist, who built moving machine sculptures, has a museum on the bank of the Rhine in Basel?
57257.e: The Museum Tinguely on the Rhine shows Jean Tinguely’s moving machine sculptures. It opened in 1996 and was designed by Mario Botta.
57257.m: The Museum Tinguely is in Basel.

57259.q: What was Winterthur especially known for in the 19th and 20th centuries?
57259.e: In Winterthur, large firms built machines, diesel engines and locomotives. The town was regarded as an industrial town.
57259.m: Winterthur was an important industrial town.

57260.q: What is the large science centre in Winterthur, where you can do experiments, called?
57260.e: At the Swiss Science Center Technorama, visitors can do experiments themselves at hundreds of stations.
57260.m: At the Technorama in Winterthur you can do experiments yourself.

57261.q: Which kind of place is Winterthur known for as a city of culture?
57261.e: Winterthur has important art collections, such as the Oskar Reinhart Collection, and a photography museum.
57261.m: Winterthur is a city of museums.

57262.e: Kyburg Castle lies south of Winterthur. In the Middle Ages it was the seat of the Counts of Kyburg.

57263.q: Which river, which also gives its name to a district of the city, flows past the edge of Winterthur?
57263.e: The Töss flows past the southern and western edge of Winterthur; one district of the city is also called Töss.
57263.m: The Töss flows along the edge of Winterthur.

57264.q: Which part of St Gallen is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
57264.e: The Abbey District with the cathedral and the Abbey Library has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983.
57264.m: The Abbey District of St Gallen is World Heritage.

57265.q: What is the Abbey Library of St Gallen world-famous for?
57265.e: The Abbey Library has thousands of manuscripts, some over 1000 years old. It is one of the oldest libraries in the world.
57265.m: Ancient manuscripts are kept in the Abbey Library.

57266.q: Which features on houses are typical of St Gallen’s old town?
57266.e: In St Gallen’s old town there are over a hundred oriel windows, often richly decorated, which wealthy merchants had built.
57266.m: St Gallen is the city of oriel windows.

57267.q: Which monk is the city of St Gallen named after?
57267.e: The monk Gall settled in the valley of the Steinach around 612. The monastery and the city of St Gallen later grew up on this spot.
57267.m: St Gallen is named after the monk Gall.

57268.q: Which speciality is traditionally eaten in St Gallen without mustard?
57268.e: The St Gallen veal bratwurst is so famous that many people think mustard would spoil its taste.
57268.m: In St Gallen people eat bratwurst without mustard.

57269.q: What is the red artwork called that covers a street in St Gallen like a living room?
57269.e: The Stadtlounge in the Bleicheli district is covered with a red surface that runs like a carpet over squares and furniture.
57269.m: The Stadtlounge turns a district into a living room.

57270.q: What is the Chapel Bridge in Lucerne mainly built from?
57270.e: The Chapel Bridge is a covered wooden bridge from the 14th century and is considered one of the oldest wooden bridges in Europe.
57270.m: The Chapel Bridge is a covered wooden bridge.

57272.q: What shape are the paintings in the roof of the Chapel Bridge?
57272.e: The gable paintings are triangular and fit under the roof. They show scenes from the history of Switzerland and Lucerne.
57272.m: Triangular paintings hang under the roof of the Chapel Bridge.

57273.q: What is the eight-sided tower next to the Chapel Bridge called?
57273.e: The Water Tower stands in the river and is older than the bridge. It used to serve as an archive, treasury and prison.
57273.m: The Water Tower stands next to the Chapel Bridge.

57274.q: Which covered wooden bridge with a water tower is the landmark of Lucerne?
57274.e: The Chapel Bridge crosses the Reuss at an angle and has an eight-sided water tower. Old paintings hang in the gable. The Spreuer Bridge is Lucerne’s second wooden bridge.
57274.m: The Chapel Bridge is the landmark of Lucerne.

57275.e: The town lies at the north-eastern end of Lake Biel, at the foot of the Jura.

57276.q: Which industry is Biel/Bienne known for around the world?
57276.e: Several large watchmakers have their headquarters in Biel/Bienne. The town is considered a watch capital.
57276.m: Biel/Bienne is a town of watches.

57277.q: Which river flows through Biel and is called the Suze in French?
57277.e: The Schüss, in French la Suze, comes from the Jura and flows through Biel into Lake Biel.
57277.m: The Schüss is called the Suze in French.

57278.q: Roughly how many inhabitants does Biel/Bienne have (as of 2023)?
57278.e: At the end of 2023, almost 56,000 people lived in Biel/Bienne. That makes it the tenth-largest town in Switzerland.

a: A core city with its suburban municipalities
57279.e: An agglomeration is a connected urban area made up of a core city and the surrounding municipalities that are closely linked to it.
57279.m: An agglomeration includes the city and its suburbs.

57280.q: What share of the Swiss population lived in an agglomeration in 2022?
57280.e: According to the Federal Statistical Office, about 74 per cent of the population lived in one of the agglomerations in 2022.
57280.m: Three out of four people in Switzerland live in an agglomeration.

57281.q: What are the municipalities around a large city where many commuters live called?
57281.e: Suburbs lie right next to the core city and form an agglomeration with it. In 2022 Switzerland had about 50 agglomerations.
57281.m: A city and its suburbs form an agglomeration.

57282.q: Which is the largest agglomeration in Switzerland?
57282.e: The Zurich agglomeration has well over a million people and is the largest in Switzerland.
57282.m: The largest agglomeration in Switzerland is Zurich.

57283.q: What do you call people who travel every day from where they live to work in another municipality?
57283.e: Many people live in the agglomeration and work in the core city. They commute back and forth every day.
57283.m: Commuters travel every day between home and work.

57284.q: Which agglomeration reaches far across the national border into France?
57284.e: Geneva is almost completely surrounded by France. Many people live in France and work in Geneva.
57284.m: The Geneva agglomeration reaches into France.

57285.q: Which means of transport links the core city of Zurich especially closely with its suburbs?
57285.e: Since 1990 the Zurich S-Bahn has linked the city with the municipalities of the agglomeration with frequent trains.
57285.m: The S-Bahn brings commuters from the agglomeration into the city.

57286.q: What is the city at the centre of an agglomeration called?
57286.e: The core city is the centre of an agglomeration; the municipalities of the agglomeration belt lie around it.
57286.m: The core city forms the centre of the agglomeration.

57287.q: Which agglomeration do the municipalities of Köniz and Ostermundigen belong to?
57287.e: Köniz and Ostermundigen border directly on the city of Bern and are closely linked with it.
57287.m: Köniz and Ostermundigen are in the Bern agglomeration.

57288.q: What is meant by urban sprawl?
a: Buildings spreading out into the countryside without order
57288.e: With urban sprawl, houses, roads and business areas spread out in a scattered way into the open countryside.
57288.m: Urban sprawl means that more and more of the countryside is built on.

57289.q: Which kind of land is mainly lost through urban sprawl in Switzerland?
57289.e: New housing is mostly built on meadows and fields on the Central Plateau. This is how valuable farmland disappears.

57290.q: Which way of building especially encourages urban sprawl?
a: Blocks of flats with several storeys
57290.e: Detached houses need a lot of land per person. When many of them are built on the edge of a village, the built-up area grows a lot.
57290.m: Estates of detached houses need a lot of land.

57291.q: What is the remedy called in which buildings are built more densely within existing settlements?
57291.e: Instead of building on new meadows, existing neighbourhoods are used better, for example with taller houses.
57291.m: Building more densely protects the countryside.

57292.q: What is the area called that a municipality has opened up for buildings?
57292.e: Normally, houses and commercial buildings may only be built in a building zone.
57292.m: As a rule, houses may only be built in the building zone.

57293.q: What did the urban sprawl initiative, rejected in 2019, want?
a: To stop making building zones any bigger
57293.e: The initiative wanted to freeze the area of building zones. Almost two thirds of voters rejected it.
57293.m: The urban sprawl initiative was rejected in 2019.

57294.q: Since the second homes initiative was accepted, what is the highest share of second homes allowed in a municipality?
57294.e: The initiative was accepted in 2012 with 50.6 per cent voting yes. Since then the share of second homes has been limited to a maximum of 20 per cent.
57294.m: At most a fifth of the homes in a municipality may be second homes.

57295.q: Which means of transport becomes especially necessary because of urban sprawl?
57295.e: In scattered settlements, shops and workplaces are far away, and buses and trains run rarely. So many people need a car.
57295.m: Urban sprawl leads to more car traffic.

57296.q: What does spatial planning control in Switzerland?
a: Where and how building is allowed
Which subjects are taught at school
57296.e: Spatial planning decides where houses, roads and factories may be built and where there is room for farming and nature. It is meant to slow down urban sprawl.
57296.m: The Spatial Planning Act is meant to slow down urban sprawl.

57297.q: Which well-known mountain village at the foot of the Matterhorn is car-free?
57297.e: No petrol cars drive in Zermatt; visitors arrive by train and use electric taxis in the village.
57297.m: Zermatt is a car-free village below the Matterhorn.

57298.q: Which settlement is considered the highest year-round inhabited settlement in Switzerland?
57298.e: Juf in the Avers valley (Grisons) lies at 2126 m above sea level and is inhabited all year round.
57298.m: Juf is the highest permanent settlement in Switzerland.

57299.q: Which group of people settled many high mountain valleys, such as the Avers, in the Middle Ages?
57299.e: The Walser emigrated from the Upper Valais and founded high-altitude settlements in the Grisons and other Alpine valleys.
57299.m: The Walser founded many high mountain villages.

57300.q: In which Engadine mountain village is the children’s book “Schellen-Ursli” (A Bell for Ursli) set?
57300.e: The book by Selina Chönz, with pictures by Alois Carigiet, is set in the village of Guarda with its painted Engadine houses.

57301.q: What does depopulation of many mountain villages describe?
a: Young people move to the valley or to towns
57301.e: Because there are not enough jobs and the journeys are long, many young people move away. As a result, some mountain villages lose inhabitants.
57301.m: Many mountain villages are struggling with depopulation.

57302.q: What is a protection forest above a mountain village for?
a: It protects against avalanches and falling rocks
It is used as a ski run
57302.e: A protection forest must not be cut down, because it protects the village from avalanches, falling rocks and landslides.
57302.m: The protection forest protects the mountain village.

57303.q: Which village in Valais was mostly buried after a glacier collapse in May 2025?
57303.e: On 28 May 2025 the Birch Glacier collapsed and buried Blatten in the Lötschental. The village had been evacuated beforehand.
57303.m: The mountain village of Blatten was buried by ice and rubble in 2025.

57304.q: Which village in the Grisons was hit by a huge rockslide on Piz Cengalo in 2017?
57304.e: In August 2017 a huge rockslide broke away from Piz Cengalo, and debris flows reached the village of Bondo in the Bregaglia.
57304.m: The rockslide on Piz Cengalo hit the village of Bondo in 2017.

57306.q: Which main region of Switzerland covers the largest area but is thinly populated?
57306.e: The Alps cover about 60 per cent of Switzerland. But because of the steep slopes and high altitudes, relatively few people live there.
57306.m: The Alps are large but thinly populated.

57307.q: Which canton has the lowest population density?
57307.e: The Grisons is the largest canton but has only about 200,000 inhabitants. Fewer than 30 people live there per square kilometre.
57307.m: The Grisons is the most thinly populated canton.

57308.q: Which canton has the highest population density?
57308.e: Basel-Stadt is very small and almost completely built up. Several thousand people live there per square kilometre.
57308.m: Basel-Stadt is the most densely populated canton.

57309.q: On average, how many people live on one square kilometre in Switzerland (as of 2024)?
57309.e: About 9 million people are spread over just over 41,000 square kilometres, which is about 220 per square kilometre.
57309.m: On average, just over 200 people live per square kilometre in Switzerland.

57310.q: Which is the largest town in the Italian-speaking part of Switzerland?
57310.e: With about 60,000 inhabitants, Lugano is the largest town in Ticino; Bellinzona, however, is the cantonal capital.
57310.m: Lugano is the largest town in Ticino.

57311.q: Which Swiss city is home to the UN’s European headquarters?
57311.e: The headquarters of the United Nations in Europe is in the Palais des Nations in Geneva.
57311.m: Geneva is a city of international organisations.

57312.q: Which town in Aargau on the Limmat has been known for its hot springs since Roman times?
57312.e: The Romans already used the warm sulphur springs in Baden and called the place Aquae Helveticae. Today there is a new thermal bath there.
57312.m: Baden is an old spa town on the Limmat.

57313.q: Which town has three castles that are a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
57313.e: The three castles Castelgrande, Montebello and Sasso Corbaro guarded the Ticino valley and have been World Heritage since 2000.
57313.m: Bellinzona is the town of three castles.

57314.q: Which of these Swiss cities has the most inhabitants?
57314.e: Basel has about 175,000 inhabitants, Winterthur about 120,000, Lucerne and St Gallen each fewer than 90,000.
57314.m: Basel is bigger than Winterthur, Lucerne and St Gallen.

57315.q: Which is the largest city in eastern Switzerland?
57315.e: St Gallen has about 76,000 inhabitants and is the most important centre of eastern Switzerland.
57315.m: St Gallen is the largest city in eastern Switzerland.

57316.q: What is the famous shopping street that runs from Zurich main station to the lake called?
57316.e: The Bahnhofstrasse links the main station with Lake Zurich and is one of the best-known shopping streets in Europe.
57316.m: The Bahnhofstrasse runs from the station to Lake Zurich.

57317.q: Which artist created the colourful choir windows in the Fraumünster in Zurich?
57317.e: In 1970 Marc Chagall designed the five choir windows of the Fraumünster in glowing colours.
57317.m: The windows in the Fraumünster are by Marc Chagall.

57318.q: What is the part of Basel on the right, northern bank of the Rhine called?
57318.e: The Rhine separates Grossbasel, with the minster, from Kleinbasel on the opposite side.
57318.m: Kleinbasel is on the right bank of the Rhine.

57319.q: What is the Basel biscuit made with honey, almonds and spices called?
57319.e: The Basler Läckerli is a hard gingerbread biscuit with honey, almonds, candied orange peel and candied lemon peel.
57319.m: The Läckerli is a Basel speciality.

57320.q: What is the oldest bridge across the Rhine in Basel called?
57320.e: The first bridge at this spot was built in the 13th century; today’s stone bridge dates from 1905.
57320.m: The Mittlere Brücke is the oldest Rhine crossing in Basel.

57321.q: Which place above Biel is home to the Swiss Federal Institute of Sport?
57321.e: In Magglingen, in French Macolin, top athletes train and PE teachers are trained.
57321.m: Magglingen above Biel is a centre of Swiss sport.

57322.q: Which island in Lake Biel was made famous by the philosopher Jean-Jacques Rousseau?
57322.e: Rousseau lived on St Peter’s Island for a few weeks in 1765 and later wrote about it with great enthusiasm.
57322.m: Rousseau made St Peter’s Island famous.

57323.q: Which well-known watch company has its headquarters in Biel/Bienne?
57323.e: The Swatch Group has its headquarters in Biel. Brands such as Omega are also based in the town.
57323.m: The watch company Swatch comes from Biel.

57324.q: What is special about Biel/Bienne compared with all other Swiss towns?
a: It is the largest bilingual town
57324.e: In Biel/Bienne, German and French are official languages with equal rights. Biel is the largest bilingual town in Switzerland.
57324.m: In Biel/Bienne people speak German and French.

57325.q: What is the medieval town wall with nine towers in Lucerne called?
57325.e: The Musegg Wall runs over the hill above the old town; some of its towers can be visited.
57325.m: The Musegg Wall once protected the town of Lucerne.

57326.q: Roughly how old is the Abbey of St Gallen?
57326.e: The monastery was founded in 719. About a hundred years earlier, the monk Gall had settled on this spot.
57326.m: The Abbey of St Gallen is about 1300 years old.

57327.q: Which famous building plan from the 9th century is kept in the Abbey Library of St Gallen?
a: The plan of St Peter’s Basilica
The plan of the Chapel Bridge
57327.e: The Plan of St Gall shows an ideal monastery and is considered the oldest surviving architectural drawing of its kind.
57327.m: The Plan of St Gall is over 1000 years old.

57328.q: Which field of study is the University of St Gallen especially known for?
57328.e: The University of St Gallen, HSG for short, is known above all for business, law and international relations.
57328.m: The HSG is a well-known business university.

57329.q: Which famous physicist published his theory of relativity in Bern in 1905?
57329.e: Albert Einstein was working at the patent office in Bern at the time; his flat on the Kramgasse is now a museum.
57329.m: Einstein developed the theory of relativity in Bern.

57330.q: Why do many more people live on the Central Plateau than in the Alps?
a: The flat land is suitable for settlements and transport
57330.e: On the hilly to flat Central Plateau, houses, roads, railway lines and fields are easy to build.
57330.m: Flat land attracts settlements and transport.

57331.q: Which lake forms the south-western border of the Swiss Central Plateau?
57331.e: The Central Plateau reaches as far as Lake Geneva in the south-west and Lake Constance in the north-east.
57331.m: Lake Geneva lies at the south-western end of the Central Plateau.

57332.q: Where do most of Switzerland’s people live today?
57332.e: Most people live in towns and their suburbs. Only a small share live in the countryside, even though rural municipalities make up more than half of the area.
57332.m: Most people in Switzerland live in towns and agglomerations.

57333.q: Which city has a metro that climbs steep slopes from the lakeshore up to the upper town?
57333.e: Lausanne’s m2 metro line runs steeply from the shore of Lake Geneva at Ouchy up into the city and beyond.
57333.m: The m2 metro in Lausanne climbs steeply from the lake to the upper town.

57334.q: What is the large square in front of Zurich Opera House, where the Böögg is burnt, called?
57334.e: The Sechseläutenplatz lies between the Opera House and Bellevue on Lake Zurich. It is one of the largest squares in the city.
57334.m: The Böögg burns on the Sechseläutenplatz.

57335.q: Which university is the largest in Switzerland by number of students?
57335.e: The University of Zurich has about 28,000 students, which makes it the largest university in the country.
57335.m: The largest university in Switzerland is in Zurich.

57336.q: What is the 126-metre-tall high-rise in Zurich West called?
57336.e: The Prime Tower was completed in 2011 and was then the tallest building in Switzerland.
57336.m: The Prime Tower shapes the skyline of Zurich West.

57337.q: What is the former industrial area in Zurich called that was turned into a district for living, offices and going out?
57337.e: There used to be factories in Zurich West. Today there are flats, offices, universities and bars and restaurants there.
57337.m: Zurich West is a converted industrial district.

57338.q: Which well-known art museum is in Riehen near Basel?
57338.e: The Fondation Beyeler shows works of classic modern art in a building by Renzo Piano.
57338.m: The Fondation Beyeler in Riehen is a famous art museum.

57339.q: Roughly how many people live on the Swiss Central Plateau?
57339.e: About 5 million people live on the Central Plateau, with about 380 inhabitants per square kilometre.
57339.m: About five million people live on the Central Plateau.

57341.q: What is the church with two pointed towers that is considered the main church of Lucerne called?
57341.e: The Hofkirche is dedicated to St Leodegar, the patron saint of Lucerne.
57341.m: The Hofkirche is the main church of Lucerne.

57342.q: Which town lies where the Aare leaves Lake Thun?
57342.e: Thun lies at the north-western end of Lake Thun; the Aare flows right through the old town below the castle.
57342.m: Thun lies where the Aare flows out of Lake Thun.

57343.q: Biel/Bienne is the urban centre of which region?
57343.e: The Seeland lies around Lakes Biel, Murten and Neuchâtel. Biel is its largest town.
57343.m: Biel/Bienne is the centre of the Seeland.

57344.q: Which famous tower with an astronomical clock stands in Bern’s old town?
57344.e: The Zytglogge used to be a town gate. Every hour on the hour its figures move, and many people watch.
57344.m: The Zytglogge is Bern’s famous clock tower.

57346.q: How many tubes does the Gotthard Base Tunnel have?
57346.e: The tunnel consists of two tubes with one track each. So the trains in each tube only travel in one direction.
57346.m: The Gotthard Base Tunnel has two tubes.

57347.q: Roughly how much did building the Gotthard Base Tunnel cost?
57347.e: The final cost was about 12.2 billion francs (as of 2016). The tunnel was paid for mainly by the Confederation.
57347.m: The Gotthard Base Tunnel cost about 12 billion francs.

57349.q: What are the many cross-passages between the two tubes of the Gotthard Base Tunnel for?
a: As escape routes into the other tube
As living space for tunnel workers
57349.e: About every 325 metres, a cross-passage links the two tubes. In an accident, passengers can escape to safety in the other tube.
57349.m: The cross-passages in the Gotthard Base Tunnel are escape routes.

57350.q: Roughly how long did it take to build the Gotthard Base Tunnel?
57350.e: The first blasting took place in 1999, and the tunnel opened after about 17 years of building.
57350.m: The Gotthard Base Tunnel took about 17 years to build.

57351.q: Roughly how much rock lies above the Gotthard Base Tunnel at the thickest point?
57351.e: Under the Gotthard massif, up to about 2450 metres of rock lie above the tunnel. There the rock is up to about 45 degrees hot.
57351.m: Up to over 2000 metres of rock lie above the Gotthard Base Tunnel.

57352.q: By roughly how much did the Gotthard Base Tunnel shorten the journey from Zurich to Lugano in 2016?
57352.e: With the Gotthard Base Tunnel, from December 2016 the journey from Zurich to Lugano took just under two hours, about 40 minutes less than before.
57352.m: The Gotthard Base Tunnel saves about 40 minutes between Zurich and Lugano.

57353.q: Why can heavier goods trains run through the Gotthard Base Tunnel than over the old mountain line?
a: There is no electricity in the tunnel.
57353.e: The old Gotthard line climbs steeply and needs extra locomotives. Through the flat tunnel, long and heavy trains can run using less power.
57353.m: Because the Gotthard Base Tunnel is almost flat, trains can carry heavy loads through it.

57354.q: Which two areas does the Lötschberg Base Tunnel link?
57354.e: The tunnel runs from Frutigen in the Bernese Oberland to Raron in Valais. This makes the train journey from Bern to Valais much faster.
57354.m: The Lötschberg Base Tunnel links the Bernese Oberland with Valais.

57355.q: What is special about the tracks in the Lötschberg Base Tunnel?
a: Most of it has only a single track.
It has three tracks side by side.
It has no tracks at all.
57355.e: Only about 40 per cent of the tunnel can be used with two tracks; the rest is single-track. This limits the number of trains.
57355.m: Much of the Lötschberg Base Tunnel has only a single track.

57356.q: Why is a base tunnel built right at the bottom of the mountain?
a: So that trains can run almost without climbing
So that the tunnel is shorter
Because it is warmer down there
So that you can see the mountains better
57356.e: A base tunnel lies at about the height of the valleys. The trains hardly have to climb and can therefore travel faster and with heavier loads.
57356.m: A base tunnel lies low down and is almost flat.

57357.q: What is missing in a section about 14 km long of the second tube of the Lötschberg Base Tunnel?
57357.e: This part of the second tube was dug out, but to save money it was not fitted with tracks and railway equipment.
57357.m: Part of the Lötschberg Base Tunnel has been dug out but has no tracks yet.

57358.q: Roughly how much did the Lötschberg Base Tunnel cost?
57358.e: In the final accounts, the total cost was put at about 5.3 billion francs.
57358.m: The Lötschberg Base Tunnel cost about 5 billion francs.

57359.q: Under which mountain range does the Lötschberg Base Tunnel run?
a: Valais Alps south of the Rhône
57359.e: The tunnel passes under the Bernese Alps between the Kander valley and the Rhône valley.
57359.m: The Lötschberg Base Tunnel runs under the Bernese Alps.

57360.q: Which railway company operates the Lötschberg Base Tunnel?
57360.e: After the SBB, BLS is the second-largest standard-gauge railway in Switzerland. Its name comes from the Bern-Lötschberg-Simplon Railway.
57360.m: The Lötschberg Base Tunnel belongs to BLS.

57361.q: What is the warm mountain water from the Lötschberg Base Tunnel used for in Frutigen?
a: For a fish farm in a tropical greenhouse
For an indoor pool with waves
57361.e: Warm water flows out of the tunnel. At the Tropenhaus Frutigen it is used to grow tropical fruit and to breed sturgeon.
57361.m: The warm tunnel water from the Lötschberg heats the Tropenhaus Frutigen.

57362.q: Which two towns in Ticino does the Ceneri Base Tunnel link?
57362.e: The Ceneri Base Tunnel lies under Monte Ceneri between the Bellinzona area and Lugano.
57362.m: The Ceneri Base Tunnel links Bellinzona with Lugano.

57363.q: Roughly how long is the Ceneri Base Tunnel?
57363.e: The Ceneri Base Tunnel is about 15.4 kilometres long. That makes it much shorter than the Gotthard tunnel.
57363.m: The Ceneri Base Tunnel is about 15 kilometres long.

57364.q: Why were tunnels on the Gotthard line enlarged by 2020 for the “4-metre corridor”?
a: So that tall lorry trailers on goods trains fit through
So that cars can drive through the railway tunnels
So that double-decker buses can drive through
So that more light gets into the tunnels
57364.e: Many lorry trailers are 4 metres high. So that they fit through the tunnels on railway wagons, tunnels and bridges from Basel to Ticino were adapted.
57364.m: In the 4-metre corridor, tall lorry trailers on goods trains fit through the tunnels.

57365.q: Who gave the go-ahead for building the NRLA in a vote in 1992?
57365.e: In Switzerland, the people often decide on large building projects. In 1992 they said yes to the New Rail Link through the Alps (NRLA).
57365.m: The voters said yes to the NRLA in 1992.

57366.q: Roughly how much did the whole NRLA cost?
57366.e: In 2017 the final cost of the NRLA was estimated at about 22.6 billion francs. This includes all the base tunnels and access lines.
57366.m: The NRLA cost a good 20 billion francs in total.

57367.q: Through which railway tunnel does the Lötschberg axis of the NRLA continue to Italy?
57367.e: The Lötschberg axis runs from Bern through the Lötschberg into Valais and then through the Simplon Tunnel to Domodossola in Italy.
57367.m: The Lötschberg axis runs through the Simplon Tunnel to Italy.

57368.q: Which two large cities does the Gotthard axis of the NRLA link?
57368.e: The Gotthard axis is the main axis of the NRLA. It runs from Zurich through the Gotthard and the Ceneri to Milan.
57368.m: The Gotthard axis of the NRLA links Zurich with Milan.

57369.q: Which NRLA tunnel is the longest railway tunnel in the world?
57369.e: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is about 57 kilometres long and opened in 2016. It is the centrepiece of the NRLA.
57369.m: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is the longest railway tunnel in the world.

57370.q: Between which two places does the Gotthard road tunnel run?
57370.e: The north entrance is near Göschenen in the canton of Uri, the south entrance near Airolo in Ticino.
57370.m: The Gotthard road tunnel runs from Göschenen to Airolo.

57371.q: Which motorway runs through the Gotthard road tunnel?
57371.e: The A2 links Basel with Chiasso and runs through the Gotthard road tunnel. It is Switzerland’s most important north-south road.
57371.m: The A2 runs through the Gotthard road tunnel.

57372.q: Which record does the Gotthard road tunnel hold?
a: Longest road tunnel in the Alps
Oldest road tunnel in the world
Widest road tunnel in the world
57372.e: At almost 17 kilometres, the Gotthard road tunnel is the longest road tunnel in the Alps.
57372.m: The Gotthard road tunnel is the longest road tunnel in the Alps.

57373.q: What happened in the Gotthard road tunnel on 24 October 2001?
a: A serious fire after a lorry accident
The opening of the second tube
57373.e: Two lorries crashed into each other and caught fire. Eleven people died, and the tunnel was closed for weeks.
57373.m: In 2001 there was a serious fire in the Gotthard road tunnel.

57374.q: Why is a second tube being built for the Gotthard road tunnel?
a: So that the old tube can be renovated
So that trains can run through the tube
So that bicycles have their own tube
So that the tunnel is shorter
57374.e: The old tube needs a thorough renovation. So that traffic is not completely cut off while this happens, a second tube is being built first.
57374.m: The second Gotthard tube makes it possible to renovate the old tunnel.

57375.q: In which year did the voters approve building a second Gotthard road tube?
57375.e: On 28 February 2016 the proposal was accepted with about 57 per cent voting yes.
57375.m: The voters said yes to the second Gotthard tube in 2016.

57376.q: When is the second tube of the Gotthard road tunnel expected to open?
57376.e: Building work has been going on since the 2020s. The opening is planned for about 2030; after that the old tube will be renovated.
57376.m: The second Gotthard tube is due to be finished around 2030.

57377.q: How does traffic flow in the Gotthard road tunnel today?
a: In both directions in one tube
On four lanes in two tubes
57377.e: Today cars drive in a single tube with one lane in each direction. Two-way traffic is especially dangerous for accidents.
57377.m: Today the Gotthard road tunnel has two-way traffic.

57378.q: What is special about the red second hand of the SBB station clock?
a: It stops briefly at the top
It only goes round once an hour
57378.e: The second hand takes a little less than a minute to go round. At the top it waits briefly until the minute hand jumps forward.
57378.m: The second hand of the SBB clock waits briefly at the top.

57379.q: What do you call the narrower track width of many mountain railways, such as the Rhaetian Railway?
57379.e: Narrow-gauge railways have less space between the rails. That lets them go round tighter bends, and they fit better into mountain valleys.
57379.m: Many mountain railways are narrow-gauge railways.

57380.q: In which city does the SBB have its headquarters?
57380.e: The headquarters of the SBB is in Bern, in the Wankdorf district. Olten is an important railway junction, but not the headquarters.
57380.m: The SBB has its headquarters in Bern.

57381.q: What do you get with the Half Fare travelcard?
57381.e: With the Half Fare travelcard you pay only half for most public transport tickets. It is one of the most popular travelcards in Switzerland.
57381.m: With the Half Fare travelcard you travel at half price.

57382.q: What was the railway project called that voters approved in 1987 and that brought faster links between the large cities?
57382.e: With Rail 2000, new lines such as Mattstetten-Rothrist were built. The aim was for trains to arrive at the big junctions shortly before the hour or half hour.
57382.m: Rail 2000 made the links between Swiss cities faster.

57383.q: At what voltage do trains run on Switzerland’s standard-gauge network?
57383.e: The overhead line of the standard-gauge railways carries alternating current at 15,000 volts and 16.7 hertz.
57383.m: The SBB overhead line carries 15,000 volts.

57384.q: What is the Italian abbreviation for the Swiss Federal Railways?
57384.e: In Italian the SBB is called “Ferrovie federali svizzere”, FFS for short. You can see this abbreviation on many trains and stations.
57384.m: In Italian the SBB is abbreviated FFS.

57385.q: What is the SBB subsidiary that transports goods called?
57385.e: SBB Cargo runs goods trains in Switzerland and carries, for example, food, building materials and post.
57385.m: SBB Cargo is responsible for the SBB’s freight traffic.

57386.q: Roughly how long is the SBB rail network?
57386.e: The SBB runs a network of about 3200 kilometres. On top of that come the lines of many other railways such as BLS or RhB.
57386.m: The SBB network is about 3200 kilometres long.

57387.q: What nickname does the Glacier Express have?
a: Slowest express train in the world
57387.e: The train travels at a leisurely pace over passes and bridges. That is why it is jokingly called the slowest express train in the world.
57387.m: The Glacier Express is known as the slowest express train in the world.

57388.q: Roughly how long does the whole journey on the Glacier Express take?
57388.e: The whole journey from Valais to the Engadine takes about eight hours.
57388.m: The Glacier Express takes about eight hours for its route.

57389.q: Which pass is the highest point on the Glacier Express route?
57389.e: The Oberalp Pass lies at 2033 m above sea level between Andermatt and Disentis. It is the highest point of the journey.
57389.m: The highest point of the Glacier Express is the Oberalp Pass.

57390.q: Between which two holiday resorts does the Glacier Express run?
57390.e: The Glacier Express links Zermatt in Valais with St Moritz in the Engadine. On the way it crosses the Oberalp Pass.
57390.m: The Glacier Express runs from Zermatt to St Moritz.

57391.q: Which two railway companies operate the Glacier Express?
a: Rhaetian Railway and Matterhorn Gotthard Railway
57391.e: The route runs over the networks of the Matterhorn Gotthard Railway in the west and the Rhaetian Railway in the east. Both run on metre gauge.
57391.m: The Glacier Express is a train of the RhB and the MGB.

57392.q: Over roughly how many bridges does the Glacier Express travel?
57392.e: On its route the Glacier Express crosses 291 bridges. On top of that there are almost a hundred tunnels.
57392.m: The Glacier Express crosses almost 300 bridges.

57393.q: Through which tunnel has the Glacier Express passed under the Furka since 1982?
57393.e: The Furka Base Tunnel opened in 1982. Since then the Glacier Express can run in winter too, because it no longer has to cross the snowy Furka.
57393.m: Since 1982 the Glacier Express has run through the Furka Base Tunnel.

57394.q: What is special about the carriages of the Glacier Express?
a: Large panoramic windows reaching into the roof
57394.e: The panoramic carriages have windows that reach far into the roof. That way you can see the mountains and glaciers especially well.
57394.m: The Glacier Express has panoramic carriages with large windows.

57395.q: What is the Italian terminus of the Bernina line called?
57395.e: Tirano lies in the Valtellina. There the narrow-gauge railway meets the Italian standard-gauge railway.
57395.m: The Bernina line ends in Tirano.

57396.q: Which pass does the Bernina line cross?
57396.e: The Bernina line runs from St Moritz over the Bernina Pass into the Val Poschiavo and on to Tirano.
57396.m: The Bernina line crosses the Bernina Pass.

57397.q: What is the panoramic train that runs to Italy on the Bernina line called?
57397.e: The Bernina Express runs from Chur or St Moritz over the Bernina Pass to Tirano. It has panoramic carriages with large windows.
57397.m: The Bernina Express runs over the Bernina Pass to Italy.

57398.e: The Bernina line is electric. It takes its power from a line above the tracks.
57398.m: The Bernina line runs on electricity.

57399.q: What is special about how the Bernina line enters Tirano?
a: It runs right across the street and square.
It goes through a glass tunnel.
It is loaded onto a ship.
57399.e: In Tirano the railway runs across the street like a tram and past the pilgrimage church. Cars then have to wait.
57399.m: In Tirano the Bernina line runs right through the town.

57400.q: What is the Bernina line among the railway lines across the Alps?
a: The highest rail crossing of the Alps
The longest rail crossing of the Alps
The oldest rail crossing of the Alps
57400.e: At the Bernina Pass the railway crosses the Alps at over 2200 m above sea level. No other railway crosses the Alps so high.
57400.m: The Bernina line is the highest railway across the Alps.

57401.q: What is the main town of the Val Poschiavo, which the Bernina line passes through, called?
57401.e: Poschiavo lies in the Italian-speaking Val Poschiavo. The railway has a large station and a workshop there.
57401.m: The Bernina line runs through Poschiavo.

57402.q: How can Bernina Express passengers travel on from Tirano to Lugano?
57402.e: From Tirano the Bernina Express Bus runs along Lake Como to Lugano. This lets you make a round trip through the Grisons and Ticino.
57402.m: From Tirano you continue to Lugano on the Bernina Express Bus.

57403.q: Where does the Rhaetian Railway have its headquarters?
57403.e: The headquarters of the Rhaetian Railway is in Chur, the capital of the Grisons.
57403.m: The Rhaetian Railway has its headquarters in Chur.

57404.q: Roughly how long is the Rhaetian Railway network?
57404.e: The RhB network is about 385 kilometres long. That makes it one of the largest narrow-gauge railways in Europe.
57404.m: The Rhaetian Railway network is about 385 kilometres long.

57405.q: Which Rhaetian Railway tunnel links the Prättigau with the Lower Engadine?
57405.e: The Vereina Tunnel is about 19 kilometres long and opened in 1999. It makes the journey to the Lower Engadine much shorter.
57405.m: The Vereina Tunnel links the Prättigau with the Lower Engadine.

57406.q: How can cars travel through the Vereina Tunnel between Klosters and the Lower Engadine?
a: On a lane of their own
Not at all, cars are banned
Only in summer on a road
57406.e: There is no road in the Vereina Tunnel. At Klosters-Selfranga, cars are loaded onto railway wagons and travel through the mountain by train.
57406.m: Cars go through the Vereina Tunnel on the car-carrying train.

57407.q: Which world record did the Rhaetian Railway set in October 2022?
a: Longest passenger train in the world
Fastest narrow-gauge train in the world
Steepest railway line in the world
57407.e: A train made of 25 multiple units, about 1.9 kilometres long, travelled over the Albula line to Alvaneu.
57407.m: In 2022 the Rhaetian Railway ran the longest passenger train in the world.

57408.q: Which Rhaetian Railway line runs from Thusis to St Moritz?
57408.e: The Albula line was built at the beginning of the 20th century. With tunnels and viaducts it overcomes big differences in height.
57408.m: The Albula line links Thusis with St Moritz.

57409.q: Which railway did the Rhaetian Railway grow out of?
57409.e: The Landquart-Davos narrow-gauge railway was founded in 1888. A few years later it was given the name Rhaetian Railway.
57409.m: The Rhaetian Railway began as a railway from Landquart to Davos.

57410.q: Where does the Rhaetian Railway get its name from?
a: From the Roman province of Raetia
57410.e: In Roman times, the area of today’s Grisons belonged to the province of Raetia. That is where the name Rhaetian Railway comes from.
57410.m: The Rhaetian Railway is named after the Roman province of Raetia.

57411.q: Roughly how high is the Rhaetian Railway’s Landwasser Viaduct?
57411.e: The Landwasser Viaduct near Filisur is about 65 metres high and 136 metres long. It was completed in 1902.
57411.m: The Landwasser Viaduct is about 65 metres high.

57412.q: In which year was the motorway vignette introduced in Switzerland?
57412.e: The vignette was introduced in 1985. The money is used to build and maintain the national roads.
57412.m: The motorway vignette has existed since 1985.

57413.q: Since which year has the Swiss motorway vignette also been available electronically as an e-vignette?
57413.e: Since August 2023 you can buy the vignette online. It is then linked to the vehicle’s number plate.

57414.q: What is the speed limit on Swiss expressways?
57414.e: Expressways are only for motor vehicles, but usually do not have separate carriageways like a motorway. The limit there is 100.
57414.m: The speed limit on Swiss expressways is 100.

57415.q: Which motorway runs from Bellinzona over the San Bernardino into the Grisons?
57415.e: The A13 links Ticino with the Rhine valley. It runs through the San Bernardino road tunnel.
57415.m: The A13 goes over the San Bernardino.

57416.q: Which motorway links Geneva, Bern, Zurich and St Gallen?
57416.e: The A1 is Switzerland’s most important east-west route. It runs from Lake Geneva to Lake Constance.
57416.m: The A1 links Geneva with St Gallen.

57417.q: Which long motorway tunnel of the A2 runs along Lake Uri?
57417.e: The Seelisberg Tunnel is about 9 kilometres long and links Beckenried in the canton of Nidwalden with Seedorf in the canton of Uri.
57417.m: The Seelisberg Tunnel takes the A2 past Lake Uri.

57418.q: How did the voters decide in November 2024 on expanding several sections of motorway?
57418.e: On 24 November 2024, about 53 per cent of voters said no to the expansion step for the national roads.
57418.m: In 2024 the voters rejected expanding the motorways.

57419.q: What do you need to be allowed to drive a car on Swiss motorways?
57419.e: The vignette is stuck on the windscreen or bought electronically. The money helps to build and maintain the national roads.
57419.m: You need a vignette on Swiss motorways.

57420.q: What must drivers form in a motorway traffic jam so that emergency vehicles can get through?
57420.e: Since 2021 forming an emergency corridor has been compulsory in Switzerland. Cars in the left lane move to the left, all others to the right.
57420.m: In a motorway traffic jam you form an emergency corridor.

57421.q: What is the three-letter IATA code of Zurich Airport?
57421.e: Every airport has a three-letter code. Zurich has ZRH, Geneva has GVA.
57421.m: Zurich Airport has the code ZRH.

57422.q: How many runways does Zurich Airport have?
57422.e: The airport has three runways between 2500 and 3700 metres long. Because some of them cross, operations are complicated.

57423.q: Roughly how many passengers used Zurich Airport in 2025?
57423.e: In 2025 Zurich Airport counted about 32.6 million passengers. There had never been so many.
57423.m: Zurich Airport had about 33 million passengers in 2025.

57424.q: Which train takes passengers underground to Dock E at Zurich Airport?
57424.e: The Skymetro is a train that glides on an air cushion. It links the main building with Dock E in the middle of the airport.
57424.m: The Skymetro runs to Dock E.

57425.q: Which airline has its main base at Zurich Airport?
57425.e: Swiss International Air Lines is the largest airline in Switzerland and has its hub in Zurich.
57425.m: Swiss has its hub in Zurich.

57426.q: What is the large complex of buildings with hotels, offices and shops right next to Zurich Airport called?
57426.e: The Circle opened in 2020. It has hotels, offices, shops, restaurants and a conference centre.
57426.m: The Circle is a large building complex at Zurich Airport.

57427.q: Until what time are planes normally allowed to take off and land at Zurich Airport?
57427.e: Flights are allowed from 6 am to 11 pm. Only to make up for delays may flights continue until 11.30 pm.
57427.m: At night there is a quiet period at Zurich Airport from 11 pm.

57428.q: Over which neighbouring country are planes not allowed to approach Zurich Airport at night and early in the morning?
57428.e: The airport is close to the border. Germany bans approaches over southern Germany at certain times to protect people from noise.
57428.m: At night, planes to Zurich may not approach over southern Germany.

57430.q: What do tanker ships bring to Switzerland along the Rhine?
57430.e: Large tanker ships bring heating oil, petrol and diesel up the Rhine to Basel. That is why the ports are important for the energy supply.
57430.m: A large share of Switzerland’s oil products comes by Rhine ship.

57431.q: Which cantons own the Swiss Rhine Ports?
57431.e: The Swiss Rhine Ports are a public institution of the two Basels. The registered office is in Birsfelden, the management in Basel.
57431.m: The Rhine Ports belong to the cantons of Basel-Stadt and Basel-Landschaft.

57432.q: Which sea do ships reach when they sail down the Rhine from Basel?
57432.e: From Basel the Rhine flows through Germany and the Netherlands. Near Rotterdam it flows into the North Sea.
57432.m: From Basel the Rhine leads to the North Sea.

57433.q: What happens at a container terminal in a port?
a: Containers are moved between ship, train and lorry
Containers are built out of wood
57433.e: At the container terminal, large cranes lift the containers from the ship onto trains or lorries and the other way round. In Basel a new terminal, Gateway Basel Nord, is planned.
57433.m: Containers are reloaded at the container terminal.

57434.q: Roughly how many containers are handled in the Rhine Ports each year?
57434.e: About 100,000 containers are handled each year at the three container terminals in Kleinhüningen.
57434.m: About 100,000 containers are handled in the Rhine Ports each year.

57435.q: How do Rhine ships on their way to Basel get past the barrages of the river power stations?
57435.e: In a lock, the ship is raised or lowered with water in a chamber. That way it gets past the dam of a power station.
57435.m: Rhine ships get past barrages through locks.

57436.q: What is special about the cog railway up Pilatus?
a: It is the steepest cog railway in the world
It is the longest railway in Switzerland
57436.e: The Pilatus Railway has a gradient of up to 48 per cent. A special rack designed by Eduard Locher stops the cogwheel from jumping out.
57436.m: The Pilatus Railway is the steepest cog railway in the world.

57437.q: Which mountain in Ticino does a cog railway climb from Capolago?
57437.e: The Monte Generoso Railway runs from Capolago on Lake Lugano to just below the summit. From the top you can see far across the Po plain.
57437.m: A cog railway runs from Capolago up Monte Generoso.

57438.q: Which viewpoint mountain above Montreux does a cog railway climb?
57438.e: The cog railway runs from Montreux via Glion up to the Rochers de Naye. From there you can see across the whole of Lake Geneva.
57438.m: A cog railway runs from Montreux up to the Rochers de Naye.

57439.q: What does a cog railway need in addition to the normal rails?
a: A toothed rack between the rails
57439.e: Normal trains move only thanks to the grip between wheel and rail. On steep lines, a cogwheel grips a toothed rack so that the train does not slip.
57439.m: A cog railway grips a toothed rack with a cogwheel.

57440.q: Which railway in the canton of Schwyz has been the steepest funicular in the world since 2017?
57440.e: The Stoosbahn climbs gradients of up to 110 per cent. Its round cabins rotate so that the floor always stays level.
57440.m: The Stoosbahn is the steepest funicular in the world.

57441.q: What makes a funicular different from an aerial cable car?
a: It runs on rails on the ground.
It hangs from a cable in the air.
57441.e: A funicular runs on rails and is pulled by a cable. With an aerial cable car, the cabins hang freely from the cable.
57441.m: A funicular runs on rails and is pulled by a cable.

57442.q: What do you call a cable car with many small cabins that keep going round in a loop?
57442.e: With a gondola lift, many small cabins travel one after another on a looping cable. You can get on almost at any time.
57442.m: A gondola lift has many small cabins on a looping cable.

57443.q: What do you call an aerial cable car in which two large cabins travel back and forth?
57443.e: With an aerial tramway, one cabin goes up while the other comes down. They pass each other in the middle.
57443.m: With an aerial tramway, two cabins travel back and forth.

57444.q: In which main region of Switzerland is most of the arable land?
57444.e: The Central Plateau is flat to hilly and has a mild climate. That is why most fields of grain, potatoes and beet are farmed there.
57444.m: Most of Switzerland’s fields are on the Central Plateau.

57445.q: Which plant is grown on the Central Plateau to make sugar?
57445.e: Swiss sugar is made from sugar beet at the sugar factories in Aarberg and Frauenfeld. Sugar cane only grows in warm, tropical countries.
57445.m: In Switzerland sugar is made from sugar beet.

57446.q: Which sector of the economy does farming belong to?
57446.e: The primary sector obtains raw materials and food directly from nature. It includes farming, forestry and fishing.
57446.m: Farming belongs to the primary sector.

57447.q: Which oil is made from the yellow-flowering fields on the Central Plateau?
57447.e: In spring the rapeseed fields on the Central Plateau glow yellow. Cooking oil is pressed from the seeds of the rapeseed.
57447.m: Yellow fields in spring are often rapeseed fields.

57448.q: Which area in the Seeland of Bern and Fribourg is called the “vegetable garden of Switzerland”?
57448.e: A great many vegetables are grown in the Grosses Moos between Lakes Biel, Neuchâtel and Murten. The fertile, dark moor soil is well suited to this.
57448.m: The Grosses Moos is the vegetable garden of Switzerland.

57449.q: Which large building project turned the marshy Seeland into fertile farmland in the 19th and 20th centuries?
57449.e: In the Jura Water Correction, the Aare was diverted into Lake Biel and the lake levels were lowered. As a result, the marshes dried out and became fields.
57449.m: The Jura Water Correction made the Seeland fertile.

57450.q: What are the payments from the Confederation to farms, for example for animal welfare and nature protection, called?
57450.e: The Confederation pays farming families direct payments for services that benefit everyone. These include caring for the landscape, biodiversity and animal-friendly farming.
57450.m: Farmers receive direct payments from the Confederation for their services.

57451.q: Which cereal is grown in Switzerland mainly for bread?
57451.e: Wheat is Switzerland’s most important bread cereal and grows mainly on the Central Plateau. Its flour is used to make bread, plaited loaves and pasta.
57451.m: Wheat is Switzerland’s most important bread cereal.

57452.q: What is it called when the decorated cattle return from the alp to the valley in autumn?
a: Alpabzug (the drive down from the alp)
57452.e: At the Alpabzug, herders and animals move down to the valley in autumn. The cows often wear flower decorations and large bells.
57452.m: At the Alpabzug, the cattle return to the valley in autumn.

57453.q: What do you call the person who looks after the cattle on the alpine pasture and makes cheese?
57453.e: The Senn or Sennin milks the cows on the alpine pasture and turns the milk into cheese. That is why the alpine hut is also called a Sennhütte.
57453.m: The Senn makes cheese on the alpine pasture.

57454.q: Why do farmers take their cattle up to the alpine pasture in summer?
a: Hay for the winter is made in the valley
It is too cold in the valley in summer
Cows are not allowed to graze in the valley
There are no flies on the alpine pasture
57454.e: While the animals eat fresh grass on the alpine pasture, the farmers can mow the meadows in the valley. That way they collect hay as winter feed.
57454.m: The alpine pasture gives the valley time for the hay harvest.

57455.q: Roughly how long does the alpine summer usually last?
57455.e: The animals usually stay on the alpine pasture from June to September, so around 100 days. After that it gets too cold up high and the grass stops growing.
57455.m: An alpine summer lasts about three months.

57456.q: What is the name of the pasture at middle altitude that is used in spring before going up to the alpine pasture?
57456.e: The Maiensäss lies between the valley floor and the alpine pasture. The cattle graze there in spring before moving higher up.
57456.m: The Maiensäss is the middle stage between valley and alpine pasture.

57457.q: What is the name for animals grazing on the alpine pasture during the summer?
57457.e: The alpine areas are officially called summering areas. Cows, cattle, sheep and goats spend the summer there.
57457.m: Summering means animals spend the summer on the alpine pasture.

57458.q: What does the dairyman in Central Switzerland call out across the alpine pasture in the evening through a wooden milk funnel?
57458.e: The alpine blessing, also called the Betruf, is a sung prayer. It is meant to protect people and animals on the alpine pasture during the night.
57458.m: With the alpine blessing the dairyman asks for protection for the alpine pasture.

57459.q: Why does alpine cheese often taste especially spicy?
a: The cows eat lots of alpine herbs
It ripens in caves made of salt
57459.e: Many different herbs and flowers grow on the alpine pastures. Their flavour passes through the milk into the cheese.
57459.m: Alpine herbs give alpine cheese its spicy taste.

57460.q: Which region in the canton of Fribourg does Gruyère come from?
57460.e: Gruyère is named after the small town of Gruyères in the Gruyère region. It is a hard cheese and carries the AOP label.
57460.m: Gruyère comes from the Gruyère region.

57461.q: What causes the holes in Emmental cheese?
57461.e: Certain bacteria produce carbon dioxide gas while the cheese ripens. The gas collects in the cheese and leaves round holes.
57461.m: The holes in Emmental are caused by gas from bacteria.

57462.q: What is Appenzeller cheese rubbed with while it ripens?
57462.e: Appenzeller is regularly treated with a herbal brine. The exact recipe is a closely guarded secret.
57462.m: Appenzeller ripens with a secret herbal brine.

57463.q: Which tool is used to scrape fine rosettes off Tête de Moine?
